question: What consent does a Level 1 GDL instruction permit require?
choices: Written consent from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P
Verbal consent from a parent at the counter
Written consent from any licensed adult over 21
A notarised letter from the applicant's school
explanation: The requirement is written consent from a parent or legal guardian, given on form DMV-DS-23P. The specific form matters — it is the same form the handbook lists among a first-time applicant's required documents.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must have written consent from a Parent or Legal Guardian on form DMV-DS-23P.

question: A 15-year-old comes to DMV with an uncle who is willing to sign for the permit. What does the handbook require?
choices: Written consent from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P
Written consent from any relative over 21
Written consent from the adult who will supervise the driving
No consent, provided the applicant has a certified birth certificate
explanation: Consent must come from a parent or legal guardian on form DMV-DS-23P. An uncle qualifies only if he is the legal guardian, and being the person who will supervise the driving is a different role with no signing authority of its own.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must have written consent from a Parent or Legal Guardian on form DMV-DS-23P.

question: On a Level 1 GDL instruction permit, who must be in the vehicle and where?
choices: A licensed driver at least 21 years old, in the right front passenger seat
A licensed driver at least 18 years old, anywhere in the vehicle
A parent or legal guardian, in any seat
A licensed driver at least 21 years old, who may sit in the back seat
explanation: The rule names both the person and the seat: a licensed driver at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat. Putting that supervisor in the back would not satisfy it, because the seat is part of the requirement, not a detail.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

question: You hold a Level 1 permit. Your 22-year-old licensed cousin rides in the back seat and your 19-year-old licensed friend sits up front. Is this permitted?
choices: No — the licensed driver who is at least 21 must be in the right front passenger seat
Yes, because a licensed driver over 21 is in the vehicle
Yes, because someone licensed is in the front passenger seat
No, because no passengers at all are allowed at Level 1
explanation: Both halves of the rule have to be satisfied at once: the supervising driver must be at least 21 and must be in the right front passenger seat. Here the 21-plus driver is in the wrong seat and the person in the right seat is too young, so neither half lines up.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

question: Which person could lawfully supervise a Level 1 permit holder?
choices: A licensed 24-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
A licensed 20-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
An unlicensed 30-year-old seated in the right front passenger seat
A licensed 24-year-old seated directly behind the driver
explanation: Three things must be true of the supervisor: licensed, at least 21, and in the right front passenger seat. The 20-year-old fails on age, the unlicensed adult fails on licensure, and the correctly aged driver in the back fails on position.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive with a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old in the right front passenger seat.

question: Between which hours may a Level 1 GDL instruction permit holder drive?
choices: 5:00 am and 10:00 pm
6:00 am and 9:00 pm
5:00 am and midnight
Sunrise and sunset
explanation: The Level 1 requirements state driving only between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm. The window is fixed by the clock, not by daylight, so it does not shift with the seasons.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive between the hours of 5:00 am and 10:00 pm.

question: It is 10:20 pm in June and still light out. Your licensed 30-year-old parent is in the right front seat. May you drive on your Level 1 permit?
choices: No — Level 1 driving is limited to the hours between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm
Yes, because a qualified supervising driver is present
Yes, because it is still light outside
Yes, provided you are driving directly home
explanation: Supervision and hours are separate restrictions and both must be met. The window closes at 10:00 pm by the clock regardless of daylight, and the handbook lists no 'driving straight home' exception at Level 1.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only drive between the hours of 5:00 am and 10:00 pm.

question: How many additional non-family passengers may a Level 1 permit holder carry?
choices: Two, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
None at all
One, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
Three, in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver
explanation: The handbook allows two additional non-family passengers in addition to the supervising licensed adult driver. The supervisor is counted separately, so the vehicle can lawfully hold the driver, the supervisor and two others.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only have two (2) additional non family passengers in addition to the supervising, licensed adult driver.

question: On your Level 1 permit, your licensed 35-year-old aunt is in the right front seat and three school friends are in the back. What is wrong?
choices: Only two additional non-family passengers are allowed besides the supervising adult
Nothing — passengers are unrestricted when a supervisor is present
The supervising adult must be a parent, not an aunt
No passengers other than the supervising adult may ride at Level 1
explanation: The limit is two additional non-family passengers on top of the supervising licensed adult driver, and three friends is one too many. The supervisor's relationship to you is not restricted — what matters is that they are licensed and at least 21.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may only have two (2) additional non family passengers in addition to the supervising, licensed adult driver.

question: What does zero tolerance mean for a Level 1 permit holder?
choices: No measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle
A blood alcohol level below 0.08
A blood alcohol level below 0.02
No alcohol consumed within eight hours of driving
explanation: The handbook spells zero tolerance out as not having any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle. It is not a lowered numeric limit and not a waiting period — measurable is the threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: ZERO Tolerance: You may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle.

question: Which statement about alcohol and a Level 1 permit holder is NOT correct?
choices: A small amount is acceptable as long as the driver is under the adult limit of 0.08
Any measurable amount of alcohol while driving violates the zero tolerance rule
The restriction applies while operating a motor vehicle
Zero tolerance is listed among the Level 1 GDL requirements
explanation: Zero tolerance replaces the adult threshold rather than sitting beneath it, so 'under 0.08' is no defence for a permit holder — any measurable amount is a violation. The other three statements track what the Level 1 requirements say.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: ZERO Tolerance: You may not have any measurable amount of alcohol in your system while operating a motor vehicle.

question: What duty does a Level 1 permit holder have regarding safety belts?
choices: To require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law
To wear a belt themselves, with passengers responsible for their own
To require belts only for passengers under 18
To require belts only for front-seat passengers
explanation: The requirement is written as a duty owed for everyone in the vehicle: you must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law. It is not limited by age or by seating position, and it makes the permit holder responsible for other people's belts as well as their own.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law.

question: Two friends get in the back of your car on your Level 1 permit and do not buckle up. Under the Level 1 requirements, whose problem is that?
choices: Yours — the permit holder must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law
Theirs alone, since each passenger is responsible for their own belt
The supervising adult's, since they are the licensed driver
No one's, because back-seat passengers are exempt
explanation: The Level 1 requirement places the duty on the permit holder to require all occupants to comply with the safety belt law. Sitting in the back does not remove a passenger from 'all occupants', and the supervising adult's presence does not transfer the duty away from you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must require all occupants to adhere to the safety belt law.

question: When may a Level 1 permit holder use a wireless communication device while driving?
choices: Only to contact a 9-1-1 system
Any time, provided it is hands-free
Only when the supervising adult is holding the phone
Only when the vehicle is moving under 25 mph
explanation: For a Level 1 permit holder the handbook allows no wireless device use while driving except for contacting a 9-1-1 system. Note this is stricter than the general hands-free rule for licensed adults — at Level 1 even hands-free use is not carved out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle, unless the use of the wireless communication device is for contacting a 9-1-1 system

question: You are driving on your Level 1 permit and want to take a hands-free call from your mother through the car's speakers. What does the handbook permit?
choices: Not this — device use is barred unless it is for contacting a 9-1-1 system
This is fine, because hands-free use is always allowed
This is fine, because a parent is calling
This is fine, because the supervising adult can answer for you
explanation: The Level 1 exception is narrow and specific: contacting a 9-1-1 system. Hands-free operation is what makes device use lawful for licensed adult drivers, but the graduated-driver rule does not repeat that carve-out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may not use a wireless communication device while operating a motor vehicle, unless the use of the wireless communication device is for contacting a 9-1-1 system

question: When does a Level 1 GDL instruction permit expire?
choices: On the applicant's 18th birthday
Six months after it is issued
On the applicant's 17th birthday
Two years after it is issued
explanation: A Level 1 permit is issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday and expires on that birthday, with a 30-day grace period allowed to complete the road skills examination. Its life is tied to your age rather than to a fixed number of months from issue.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 1 GDL instruction permit will be issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday, and will expire on the 18th birthday.

question: Which statement correctly describes the life of a Level 1 GDL instruction permit?
choices: It runs up to the 18th birthday and expires then, with a 30-day grace period for the road skills examination
It runs for six months and can be renewed twice
It runs until the holder passes the road skills test, with no expiry
It runs to the 21st birthday
explanation: The handbook ties expiry to the 18th birthday and adds a 30-day grace period beyond it so there is time to complete the Road Skills Examination. It is also nonrenewable, so the grace period is the only extension the handbook describes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 1 GDL instruction permit will be issued up to the applicant's 18th birthday, and will expire on the 18th birthday.

question: Who is eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license?
choices: Someone between 16 and 18 who has completed all the Level 1 GDL requirements
Anyone 15 or older who has held a permit for 30 days
Anyone under 18 who has passed a road skills test
Someone between 17 and 21 who has completed driver's education
explanation: The handbook sets the gate at being between 16 and 18 and having completed all the Level 1 requirements. Age alone is not enough, and completing Level 1 requirements without reaching 16 is not enough either.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you are between the ages of 16 and 18 and have completed all the requirements of the Level 1 GDL instruction permit, you will be eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license.

question: A 15-year-old has held a Level 1 permit for eight conviction-free months and completed a 50-hour driving log. Can they move to Level 2?
choices: No — Level 2 eligibility starts at 16
Yes, because the time and log requirements are met
Yes, but only with additional parental consent
No, because 12 conviction-free months are required
explanation: Time served and the driving log are necessary but not sufficient: the handbook opens Level 2 to applicants between 16 and 18. The 12-month conviction-free requirement belongs to the step from Level 2 to Level 3, not this one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you are between the ages of 16 and 18 and have completed all the requirements of the Level 1 GDL instruction permit, you will be eligible for a Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license.

question: How much conviction-free driving at Level 1 is required before applying for Level 2?
choices: A minimum of 180 consecutive days immediately preceding the application
A minimum of 90 consecutive days
A minimum of 12 months
A minimum of 30 days
explanation: The handbook requires a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 immediately preceding the Level 2 application. Both 'consecutive' and 'immediately preceding' matter, because a conviction breaks the run and it has to be rebuilt.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 GDL immediately preceding the date of your Level 2 application

question: Which of these would satisfy the Level 1 time requirement for a Level 2 application?
choices: 180 consecutive conviction-free days ending on the day of the application
200 days on a permit that included a conviction 60 days ago
180 days spread over two separate permits
90 conviction-free days plus a driver's education course
explanation: The requirement is 180 consecutive conviction-free days immediately before the application, so a conviction 60 days ago restarts the count and leaves the applicant well short. Driver's education substitutes for the 50-hour log, not for the conviction-free period.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a minimum of 180 consecutive days of conviction-free driving at Level 1 GDL immediately preceding the date of your Level 2 application

question: What behind-the-wheel evidence does Level 2 require?
choices: A certified log of at least 50 hours including at least 10 at night, or an approved driver's education course
A certified log of at least 30 hours including 5 at night
A certified log of at least 50 hours, all of which may be in daylight
An instructor's letter confirming 20 hours of practice
explanation: The handbook asks for a parent or legal guardian certified log sheet of at least 50 hours behind the wheel including at least 10 hours at night, and offers an approved driver's education course as the alternative. The night hours are part of the 50, not extra.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a parent or legal guardian certification (log sheet) of  a minimum  of 50 hours behind the wheel, including the  minimum of 10 hours at night or complete a driver's education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education

question: A Level 1 permit holder has logged 52 hours of driving, all of it after school before dark. What is the problem?
choices: At least 10 of the 50 hours must be at night
Nothing — 52 hours exceeds the 50-hour requirement
The log must show 60 hours if no driver's education course was taken
Only hours supervised by a certified instructor count
explanation: Hitting the hour total is not enough because the handbook specifies at least 10 of those hours at night. The alternative route is completing an approved driver's education course, which replaces the log requirement entirely.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Have a parent or legal guardian certification (log sheet) of  a minimum  of 50 hours behind the wheel, including the  minimum of 10 hours at night or complete a driver's education course approved by the West Virginia Department of Education

question: Between which hours must a Level 2 holder have a supervising licensed adult aged 21 or older?
choices: 10:00 pm and 5:00 am
9:00 pm and 6:00 am
Midnight and 5:00 am
Sunset and sunrise
explanation: Level 2 allows unsupervised driving between 5:00 am and 10:00 pm, which means the supervised window is 10:00 pm to 5:00 am. The supervisor must be a licensed adult aged 21 or older — the same standard as at Level 1.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license must drive with a supervising, licensed adult driver who is age 21 or older between the hours of 10:00 pm and 5:00 am.

question: It is 11:30 pm and a Level 2 holder is driving home from a friend's house alone. How does the handbook treat this?
choices: It breaks the rule, because between 10:00 pm and 5:00 am a supervising licensed adult 21 or older is required
It is allowed, because a Level 2 holder may drive alone at any hour
It is allowed, because driving home is always an exception
It is allowed if the driver is within a few miles of home
explanation: Unsupervised Level 2 driving stops at 10:00 pm. The handbook does list four exceptions to the night rule, but visiting a friend is not among them — they are lawful employment, school-sanctioned activities, religious activities, and emergencies to prevent injury or death.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license must drive with a supervising, licensed adult driver who is age 21 or older between the hours of 10:00 pm and 5:00 am.

question: Which of these is one of the handbook's exceptions to the Level 2 night-driving rule?
choices: Going to, taking part in, or returning from lawful employment
Driving a family member's vehicle rather than your own
Driving on roads posted at 35 mph or less
Driving with another Level 2 holder in the passenger seat
explanation: The four exceptions are lawful employment, a school-sanctioned activity, a religious activity, and an emergency to prevent bodily injury or death. Each covers going to, participating in, or returning from the activity, so the drive home from a shift is included.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

question: Which of the following is NOT an exception to the Level 2 night-driving restriction?
choices: Driving friends home after a party
Returning from a school-sanctioned activity
Driving to a religious activity
Driving in an emergency to prevent bodily injury or the death of another
explanation: The handbook's four exceptions are lawful employment, school-sanctioned activities, religious activities and emergencies to prevent injury or death. A social occasion is not on the list, and adding passengers does not make the drive lawful.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

question: A Level 2 holder finishes a shift at a restaurant at 11:15 pm and drives straight home alone. How does the handbook treat that drive?
choices: It falls within the lawful employment exception to the night-driving rule
It breaks the rule, because the exception covers only the drive to work
It breaks the rule, because all night driving requires a supervising adult
It is allowed only if the employer signs a letter
explanation: The exception is written to cover going to, participating in, and returning from lawful employment, so the drive home after a shift is included. That wording is the reason a work trip is treated differently from a social one at the same hour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The exceptions to this rule are when the licensee is participating in, going to, or returning from: (1) lawful employment; (2) a school-sanctioned activity; (3) a religious activity; or (4) an emergency situation that requires the licensee to prevent bodily injury or the death of another.

question: During the first six months at Level 2, which passengers are barred?
choices: Any non-family member under the age of 20
Any passenger under the age of 18
All passengers other than a parent or guardian
Any non-family member under the age of 16
explanation: For the first six months a Level 2 holder may not drive with any non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger. The test is the passenger's age and whether they are family — not your own age, and not how many of them there are.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license holder may not operate a motor vehicle during their first six months with any non-family members under the age of 20 as a passenger

question: During the second six months at Level 2, how many non-family passengers under 20 are allowed?
choices: One
None
Two
Any number, once the first six months have passed
explanation: The limit relaxes rather than disappears: no more than one non-family member under the age of 20 during the second six months. The restriction only ends when the driver moves beyond Level 2.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: may not operate a motor vehicle with more than one (1) non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger during the second six (6) months.

question: You have held a Level 2 licence for eight months. Your 16-year-old brother and your 17-year-old neighbour both want a ride at 4:00 pm. What does the handbook allow?
choices: Both may ride — your brother is family, and the neighbour is your one permitted non-family passenger under 20
Neither may ride until you reach Level 3
Only your brother may ride, because no non-family passengers are allowed at Level 2
Both may ride, because the passenger restriction ends after six months
explanation: Family members are outside the count, so your brother does not use up the allowance. In the second six months you may carry one non-family member under 20, and the neighbour fills exactly that slot. The hour is fine because 4:00 pm sits inside the 5:00 am to 10:00 pm unsupervised window.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: may not operate a motor vehicle with more than one (1) non-family member under the age of 20 as a passenger during the second six (6) months.

question: Three months into Level 2, a driver gives a 19-year-old teammate a lift to practice. Why is that a problem?
choices: In the first six months no non-family member under 20 may ride as a passenger
It is not a problem, because the teammate is over 18
It is a problem only if more than one teammate rides along
It is a problem only after 10:00 pm
explanation: The first-six-months rule bars any non-family passenger under the age of 20, and a 19-year-old is under 20. The one-passenger allowance does not begin until the second six months, and the time of day is a separate restriction that does not soften this one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license holder may not operate a motor vehicle during their first six months with any non-family members under the age of 20 as a passenger

question: Which Level 1 restrictions continue to apply at Level 2?
choices: No measurable alcohol, and the duty to require all occupants to follow the seat belt law
The 10:00 pm curfew with no exceptions, and the two-passenger limit
Driving only with a licensed adult 21 or older at all times
Neither — Level 2 removes all Level 1 restrictions
explanation: The handbook says that as with Level 1 permit drivers, a Level 2 holder may not drive with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law. Level 2 loosens supervision and passengers, but not alcohol or belts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license may not operate a motor vehicle with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law.

question: A 17-year-old Level 2 holder has one drink at a family dinner and drives home at 8:00 pm. How does the handbook treat this?
choices: It violates the rule against operating with any measurable alcohol in the system
It is allowed, because the driver is under the 0.08 adult limit
It is allowed, because a family member served the drink
It is allowed, because the driving happened before 10:00 pm
explanation: The Level 2 standard is any measurable alcohol, not a number below the adult threshold. Where the alcohol came from and what time it is do not enter into it — the hours restriction is a separate rule that this driver happened to satisfy.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license may not operate a motor vehicle with any measurable alcohol in their system and must require all occupants to follow the seat belt law.

question: What happens if a driver under 18 surrenders a Level 2 intermediate licence for any reason?
choices: They must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit
They may reapply for Level 2 after 30 days
They keep their place and reapply for Level 2 immediately
They move directly to a Level 3 GDL at 18
explanation: The handbook states that surrendering a Level 2 licence for any reason while under 18 means starting over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit. 'For any reason' is broad — it is not limited to surrenders connected with a violation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you surrender your Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license for any reason and are under the age of 18, you must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

question: Which statement about surrendering a Level 2 licence is NOT correct?
choices: The driver may resume at Level 2 as soon as they reapply
A driver under 18 must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit
The rule applies when the licence is surrendered for any reason
Starting over means meeting the Level 1 requirements again
explanation: Starting over is exactly what the handbook requires — a Level 1 instruction permit again, not a fresh Level 2. The rule is triggered by surrender for any reason while the driver is under 18.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you surrender your Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license for any reason and are under the age of 18, you must start over with a Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

question: How does a conviction affect the six-month conviction-free period at Level 1?
choices: The six-month window starts over from the date of the conviction
The window pauses and resumes once any fine is paid
The window is shortened by 30 days as a penalty
The window is unaffected unless there are two convictions
explanation: The handbook says that with each conviction the six-month window starts over from the date of the conviction. It resets rather than pausing, which means a conviction late in the period costs you the whole period, not a few days.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You must be conviction-free for 6 months in order to graduate to a Level 2 Intermediate driver's license.  With each conviction the 6-month window starts over from the date of the conviction.

question: A Level 1 permit holder is five months into their conviction-free period when they are convicted of a violation. How much longer must they wait for Level 2?
choices: A further six months, counted from the date of the conviction
One more month, completing the original six
Three more months, as a half-period penalty
No extra time, because only two convictions matter
explanation: Because the window restarts from the conviction date, the five months already served are gone and a fresh six months begins. That reset is what makes a single early ticket so expensive for a graduated driver.

question: What happens after two convictions on a Level 1 GDL instruction permit?
choices: The permit is revoked for 90 days, after which you must re-apply and retest
The permit is suspended for 30 days and then returned automatically
The holder moves straight to a Level 2 probationary licence
A warning letter is sent but the permit stays valid
explanation: Two convictions revoke the Level 1 GDL for 90 days, and when the 90 days are up the handbook requires you to re-apply and retest for the Level 1 permit. The revocation is not self-clearing — the testing has to be done again.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: Under a Level 1 GDL instruction permit, two (2) convictions will result in the revocation of your GDL for 90 days. When 90 days are up you will be required to re-apply and retest for your Level 1 GDL instruction permit.

question: A Level 1 permit holder has their permit revoked after a second conviction. Ninety days later, what must happen before they can drive again on a permit?
choices: They must re-apply and retest for the Level 1 GDL instruction permit
The permit is reinstated automatically at the end of the 90 days
They must wait until their 18th birthday
They may apply directly for a Level 2 intermediate licence
explanation: The handbook is explicit that when the 90 days are up you are required to re-apply and retest for the Level 1 permit. Serving the revocation period restores eligibility to apply, not the permit itself.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: How long must a Level 2 holder be conviction-free before graduating to Level 3?
choices: 12 months
6 months
180 days
24 months
explanation: Level 2 to Level 3 requires 12 conviction-free months, and a conviction restarts that 12-month period from the point of the conviction. The six-month and 180-day figures belong to the earlier step from Level 1 to Level 2.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You are required to be conviction-free for 12 months prior to graduating to a  Level 3 GDL.  If you receive a conviction, the 12-month conviction-free period will start over again at the point of  that conviction.

question: Which pairing of level and conviction-free period is correct?
choices: Level 2 to Level 3 requires 12 conviction-free months
Level 1 to Level 2 requires 12 conviction-free months
Level 2 to Level 3 requires 6 conviction-free months
Level 1 to Level 2 requires 24 conviction-free months
explanation: The handbook uses six months for the Level 1 to Level 2 step and 12 months for the Level 2 to Level 3 step. Keeping the two apart is easier if you remember that the more freedom the level grants, the longer the clean record it demands.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: You are required to be conviction-free for 12 months prior to graduating to a  Level 3 GDL.  If you receive a conviction, the 12-month conviction-free period will start over again at the point of  that conviction.

question: What does a second conviction for a moving violation at Level 2 require?
choices: Revocation of the driving privilege until age 18, and retesting as a first-time applicant
A 90-day suspension followed by automatic reinstatement
Enrollment in a driver improvement program only
Demotion to a Level 1 instruction permit for 30 days
explanation: The handbook requires revocation of the driving privilege until you are 18 and then retesting as a first-time applicant. Enrollment in a driver improvement program is the consequence of the first conviction, not the second.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: The second conviction for a moving violation requires the revocation of your driving privilege until you are 18 and you will be required to retest as a first-time applicant.

question: A 16-year-old Level 2 holder is convicted of a second moving violation. What is the practical effect?
choices: No driving privilege until 18, and then the full first-time applicant testing process
A three-month suspension, after which Level 2 resumes
Automatic demotion to Level 1 with the original permit restored
A fine only, with the licence unaffected
explanation: Because revocation runs until age 18, a 16-year-old loses roughly two years of driving. On top of that the handbook requires retesting as a first-time applicant, so the driver re-enters the system at the beginning rather than where they left off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: The second conviction for a moving violation requires the revocation of your driving privilege until you are 18 and you will be required to retest as a first-time applicant.

question: What effect does a cell phone or wireless device citation have on a Level 1 or Level 2 driver?
choices: The conviction-free time period must begin over again
It carries a fine but does not affect the conviction-free period
It adds 30 days to the conviction-free period
It applies only to Level 2 drivers
explanation: The handbook states that a citation for cell phone or wireless device use on a Level 1 or Level 2 GDL means you must begin the conviction-free time period over — six months at Level 1, twelve at Level 2. It is treated like any other conviction for clock purposes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions
source.sourceQuote: If a citation is issued for the use of a cell phone or wireless communication device on a Level 1 GDL instruction permit or Level 2 GDL intermediate driver's license, you must begin the conviction-free time period over

question: A Level 2 driver ten months into a clean twelve months is cited for texting. What has it cost them?
choices: The twelve-month conviction-free period starts over, so Level 3 is at least a year away again
Two months, which are added to the end of the period
Nothing, because phone citations carry no points
Their licence is revoked until 18
explanation: The conviction-free period begins over rather than being extended, so ten months of clean driving are wiped out. Revocation until 18 is the penalty for a second moving-violation conviction at Level 2, which is a separate and harsher consequence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Levels 1 and 2 GDL Violations and Convictions

question: What must be true to be eligible for a Level 3 GDL?
choices: 12 months of conviction-free driving at Level 2, being at least 17, and completing all requirements
6 months of conviction-free driving at Level 2, and being at least 16
12 months at Level 2 and being at least 18
Passing a second road skills test at any age
explanation: The handbook sets three conditions together: 12 conviction-free months at Level 2, a minimum age of 17, and successful completion of all requirements. The age floor rises by one at each stage — 15, 16, 17.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: To be eligible for a Level 3 GDL, you must have completed 12 months of conviction-free driving under a Level 2 GDL, be at least 17 years old, and have successfully completed all requirements.

question: A driver turns 17 having held Level 2 for eight conviction-free months. Are they eligible for Level 3?
choices: No — 12 conviction-free months at Level 2 are required as well as being 17
Yes, because they have reached the minimum age of 17
Yes, because eight months exceeds the six-month requirement
No, because Level 3 is only available at 18
explanation: Age and time are cumulative requirements, not alternatives: the driver meets the age test but is four months short on the conviction-free period. The six-month figure belongs to the Level 1 to Level 2 step and does not apply here.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: To be eligible for a Level 3 GDL, you must have completed 12 months of conviction-free driving under a Level 2 GDL, be at least 17 years old, and have successfully completed all requirements.

question: How are West Virginia cards for applicants under 21 printed?
choices: Vertically — red for ages 15 to 17 and blue for ages 18 to 20
Horizontally, with a red border for anyone under 21
Vertically and blue for everyone under 21
Vertically and red for everyone under 21
explanation: The handbook describes two vertical formats under 21: red for 15 to 17 and blue for 18 to 20. The colour and orientation exist so law enforcement and retailers can see the cardholder's age bracket immediately.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants 15 to 17 years old are issued a driver's license or instruction permit that is vertical and color-coded red.  Applicants 18 to 20 years old, are issued a vertical driver's license or instruction permit that is color-coded blue.

question: A cashier is handed a vertical, red-coded West Virginia licence. What does that tell them about the holder's age bracket?
choices: The holder is between 15 and 17
The holder is between 18 and 20
The holder is 21 or over
The card carries a restriction code
explanation: Red vertical cards are issued to applicants 15 to 17 and blue vertical cards to applicants 18 to 20, which is why the handbook says the design alerts officials and retailers to the holder's age. Applicants 21 and over get a horizontal card instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants 15 to 17 years old are issued a driver's license or instruction permit that is vertical and color-coded red.  Applicants 18 to 20 years old, are issued a vertical driver's license or instruction permit that is color-coded blue.

question: Where does a restriction appear on a West Virginia driver's license?
choices: As a number or letter code in the restrictions field on the front, explained on the back
As a full sentence printed on the front of the card
Only in the DMV's records, not on the card
As a coloured stripe along the edge of the card
explanation: The handbook describes a code in the restrictions field on the front, with the explanation of that code on the back of the card. This matters because a code alone does not tell you what it means — you have to read the reverse.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The restriction will be indicated on the front of the driver's license by a number or letter code in the “restrictions” field.  The explanation of the restriction will appear on the back of the driver's license.

question: You are handed a licence with a code in the restrictions field and want to know what it means. Where does the handbook say to look?
choices: On the back of the driver's license
In the DMV Online Services portal only
On the front of the card, beneath the photograph
On the vehicle registration card
explanation: The explanation of a restriction appears on the back of the licence, while the code itself is in the restrictions field on the front. Driving in violation of a restriction is treated as a serious offense, so knowing how to read the code matters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The restriction will be indicated on the front of the driver's license by a number or letter code in the “restrictions” field.  The explanation of the restriction will appear on the back of the driver's license.

question: Under the Drive for Five program, when do West Virginia driver's licenses expire?
choices: In a year in which the holder's age is divisible by five
Exactly five years after the date of issue, whatever the holder's age
At the end of the month in which the holder's birthday falls
In a year in which the holder's age is divisible by two
explanation: Drive for Five ties expiry to age: the licence runs out in a year when your age divides by five, such as 25, 30 or 35. Once you are inside the cycle the licence is valid for five years, but the phase-in period can be three to seven years depending on your age at renewal.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under the “Drive for Five” program, all driver's  licenses will expire in a year in which your age is divisible by five (for example, age 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, etc.).

question: A driver renews at 32. Under Drive for Five, in which year will the new licence expire?
choices: The year the driver turns 35
The year the driver turns 37
The year the driver turns 40
Exactly five years later, whatever their age at the time
explanation: Expiry falls in a year when age is divisible by five, and the next such year after 32 is 35. This is also why an initial licence can run anywhere from three to seven years — DMV uses that first card to phase the driver into the five-year cycle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Under the “Drive for Five” program, all driver's  licenses will expire in a year in which your age is divisible by five (for example, age 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, etc.).

question: How long do you have to notify the DMV of an address change, and in what form?
choices: Within 20 days, in writing
Within 30 days, by phone or in writing
Within 60 days, in writing
At your next renewal, in person
explanation: The handbook requires written notice to the DMV within 20 days of the change, and states that failing to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment. Notifying the Post Office does not update your DMV record or forward DMV mail.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you change your address you are required to notify, in writing, the DMV within 20 days of the change. Failure to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment.

question: You move across town and file a change of address with the Post Office. What does the handbook say about your DMV record?
choices: It is unchanged — you must still notify the DMV in writing within 20 days
The Post Office notifies the DMV automatically
It updates when your mail is first forwarded
No notice is needed for a move within the same county
explanation: The handbook states that simply notifying the U.S. Post Office will not update your DMV record or allow important DMV mail to be forwarded. The written 20-day notice is separate, and missing it risks a fine or imprisonment as well as missed renewal and suspension notices.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you change your address you are required to notify, in writing, the DMV within 20 days of the change. Failure to do this subjects you to a possible fine or imprisonment.

question: How long does a new resident who wants to drive have to apply for a WV driver's license?
choices: 30 days after establishing residency
90 days after establishing residency
6 months after establishing residency
Until their out-of-state licence expires
explanation: The handbook gives new residents 30 days from establishing WV residency to apply. That is separate from the 90-day nonresident exemption, which applies to people who have not become residents at all.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: After establishing WV residency, new residents who want to drive in WV must apply for a WV driver's license within 30 days.

question: Which driver is working under the 30-day rule rather than the 90-day nonresident exemption?
choices: Someone who has just moved to WV and taken a local address
A visitor from Ohio staying two months with relatives
An out-of-state student attending a WV university
A service member from another state stationed briefly in WV
explanation: The 30-day rule is written for new residents, so establishing residency is what triggers it. The other three keep their nonresident status and fall under the exemptions instead, which is why the two time limits are easy to confuse.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: After establishing WV residency, new residents who want to drive in WV must apply for a WV driver's license within 30 days.

question: What does the handbook require in order to transfer a valid out-of-state driver's license?
choices: Pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender the out-of-state licence
Pass the knowledge and road skills tests again
Surrender the out-of-state licence only
Pass a vision screening only
explanation: Three steps are listed: the vision screening, a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrendering the out-of-state licence before a WV licence is issued. A valid out-of-state licence spares you the knowledge and road tests, not the screening and course.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender your out-of-state driver's license before a WV driver's license will be issued.

question: Which statement about transferring a valid out-of-state licence is NOT correct?
choices: You may keep your old licence as a souvenir once the WV licence is issued
You must pass a vision screening
You must complete a brief alcohol awareness course
A transfer applicant must present the documents required of a first-time applicant
explanation: The handbook requires you to surrender the out-of-state licence before a WV licence will be issued, so keeping it is not an option. The vision screening, the alcohol awareness course and the first-time applicant document list all apply to transfers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You are required to pass a vision screening, complete a brief alcohol awareness course, and surrender your out-of-state driver's license before a WV driver's license will be issued.

question: A West Virginia licence that has been expired for how long requires retesting?
choices: Three years or more
One year or more
Six months or more
Five years or more
explanation: The handbook sets the line at three years or more expired, including for a CDL, and requires retesting past it. The same three-year line governs whether an out-of-state licence can be transferred or must be re-earned from scratch.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any person renewing a WV driver's license, including a CDL, that has been expired for three (3) years or more is required to retest.

question: Someone returns to West Virginia with a WV licence that expired four years ago. What should they expect?
choices: To retest, because the licence has been expired three years or more
To renew over the counter with a late fee
To renew after a vision screening only
To be treated as a transfer applicant from another state
explanation: Four years past expiry is beyond the three-year line, so the handbook requires retesting rather than a simple renewal. They are not a transfer applicant either — that route is for a licence issued by another state or jurisdiction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Any person renewing a WV driver's license, including a CDL, that has been expired for three (3) years or more is required to retest.

question: How does the handbook describe responsibility for your actions behind the wheel?
choices: The privilege to drive carries many responsibilities, and you and only you are responsible for your actions
Responsibility is shared between the driver and the vehicle's owner
A supervising adult is responsible for a young driver's actions
Responsibility passes to the insurer once a policy is in force
explanation: The chapter opens by calling driving a privilege that carries many responsibilities and states that you, and only you, are responsible for your actions. Insurance and supervision change who pays or who rides along, not who is responsible for the driving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The privilege to drive carries with it many responsibilities.  You, and only you, are responsible for your actions.

question: Which statement is NOT how the handbook frames the driving privilege?
choices: Driving is a right that cannot be taken away once a licence is issued
Driving is a privilege that carries many responsibilities
You and only you are responsible for your actions
There are requirements a licence holder must be aware of to keep the privilege
explanation: The handbook consistently uses the language of privilege, not right, and the whole chapter is about requirements you must meet to maintain that privilege. Calling it an untouchable right contradicts every suspension and revocation rule that follows.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The privilege to drive carries with it many responsibilities.  You, and only you, are responsible for your actions.

question: What can happen if a minor's school notifies the DMV of non-attendance or excessive unexcused absences?
choices: The licence is further restricted to work, medical, educational and religious purposes until age 18 or reinstatement
The licence is revoked permanently
The DMV takes no action until the student turns 18
The student is fined but keeps a full licence
explanation: A school report of non-attendance or excessive unexcused absences leads the DMV to restrict the licence to limited purposes until age 18, or until the student presents a school reinstatement authorization form and pays the reinstatement fee. It is a restriction with a route back, not a permanent loss.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences

question: A 16-year-old has a restricted licence after their school reported excessive absences. What does the handbook say ends the restriction?
choices: Turning 18, or presenting a school reinstatement authorization form and paying the reinstatement fee
Passing the knowledge test again
Waiting six months with no further absences
A parent's written request to the DMV
explanation: The handbook gives two exits: reaching age 18, or producing a reinstatement authorization form from the school along with the reinstatement fee. The school that reported the problem is also the body that authorises the way back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your school notifies the DMV that you are not attending or have excessive unexcused absences

question: When can the DMV require an existing licence holder to take a medical, written or driving examination?
choices: When the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe the driver is incompetent or otherwise not qualified
Only after a crash involving injury
Only when the driver reaches age 70
Only if the driver has 12 or more points
explanation: The trigger is the Commissioner having good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed. It is not tied to age, points or a crash, and refusing to submit to the examination is itself grounds for suspension or revocation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may be required to take a medical, written, or driving examination if the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed.

question: A driver is told to report for a re-examination and simply refuses to attend. What does the handbook say follows?
choices: Refusal is grounds for suspension or revocation of the driver's license
Nothing, because the examination is voluntary
A fine, after which the matter is closed
The licence is restricted to daylight driving only
explanation: Refusal to submit to the test is expressly grounds for suspension or revocation. The examination exists because the Commissioner already has good cause to doubt the driver's qualification, so declining it resolves nothing in the driver's favour.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may be required to take a medical, written, or driving examination if the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe you are incompetent or otherwise not qualified to be licensed.

question: Which crashes must be reported, and within what time?
choices: Those causing injury or death, or property damage over $1,000 — within five days by the quickest means possible
Only crashes involving injury — within ten days
All crashes without exception — within 24 hours
Those causing property damage over $5,000 — within thirty days
explanation: The handbook sets the threshold at injury, death, or property damage in excess of $1,000, and gives five days to report by the quickest means possible, oral or written. Both parts of the threshold matter: an injury triggers the duty no matter how small the damage.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Crashes resulting in injury to, or death of, any person or property damage in excess of $1,000 must be reported by the quickest means possible (oral or written) within five (5) days to the local police department if it occurs within a municipality

question: A crash happens outside any municipality and causes $1,500 in damage. Who must the report go to?
choices: The county sheriff or the nearest WV State Police office
The local police department of the nearest town
The DMV in Charleston only
Your insurance company, which reports it on your behalf
explanation: The handbook splits reporting by location: the local police department if the crash occurs within a municipality, otherwise the county sheriff or the nearest WV State Police office. Insurers and the DMV are not named as the recipient of the crash report.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Crashes resulting in injury to, or death of, any person or property damage in excess of $1,000 must be reported by the quickest means possible (oral or written) within five (5) days to the local police department if it occurs within a municipality

question: What happens if you were uninsured on the date of a reportable crash?
choices: Your motor vehicle registration and your driving privilege will be suspended
You are fined but keep your licence and registration
Only the registration is suspended
Nothing, provided you pay for the damage yourself
explanation: Being without the required WV liability insurance on the date of the crash suspends both the registration and the driving privilege. Paying the other party does not cure it, because the obligation is to have carried the coverage at the time.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of the crash, your motor vehicle registration and driving privilege will be suspended.

question: Your policy lapsed two weeks before a minor collision that you report properly. Why is reporting it correctly not the end of the matter?
choices: Because being uninsured on the date of the crash suspends both your registration and your driving privilege
Because reporting late always carries a separate penalty
Because a lapsed policy only matters if someone is injured
Because the DMV cannot verify coverage retroactively
explanation: Reporting satisfies the crash-reporting duty, but insurance is a separate obligation measured on the date of the crash. The handbook also notes the DMV verifies coverage electronically with insurers, so a lapse is not something a clean report conceals.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle was not covered by the required West Virginia liability insurance on the date of the crash, your motor vehicle registration and driving privilege will be suspended.

question: What does West Virginia law require of motorists driving on public roads?
choices: They must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance
They must carry either insurance or a cash deposit with the DMV
They must carry collision coverage on the vehicle
They must carry insurance only if the vehicle is financed
explanation: The handbook states the mandate plainly: all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance. Liability coverage is what protects other people, which is why it is the coverage the state compels.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law mandates that all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance.

question: Which driver is complying with the compulsory insurance law as the handbook states it?
choices: A driver on a public road carrying WV motor vehicle liability insurance
A driver carrying only comprehensive coverage for theft and fire
A driver who has applied for insurance but has no policy yet
A driver who owns the vehicle outright and therefore carries none
explanation: The requirement is specifically West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance. Other kinds of coverage protect your own property rather than other road users, and owning the vehicle outright does not exempt anyone from the mandate.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia law mandates that all motorists driving on the state's public roads must carry West Virginia motor vehicle liability insurance.

question: What are the minimum liability coverage amounts provided by law?
choices: $25,000 for one death or injury, $50,000 for two, and $25,000 for property damage
$50,000 for one death or injury, $100,000 for two, and $50,000 for property damage
$10,000 for one death or injury, $20,000 for two, and $10,000 for property damage
$25,000 combined for all injuries and property damage
explanation: The handbook lists three separate minimums: $25,000 for one death or injury, $50,000 for two deaths or injuries, and $25,000 for property damage. They are separate limits rather than one combined pot.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: $25,000 for one (1) death or injury | $50,000 for two (2) deaths or injuries | $25,000 for property damage

question: Which statement about the minimum coverage figures is NOT correct?
choices: A single $25,000 limit covers injuries and property damage together
The minimum for one death or injury is $25,000
The minimum for two deaths or injuries is $50,000
The minimum for property damage is $25,000
explanation: The handbook sets out three distinct minimums rather than one combined figure, which is why the property damage limit and the single-injury limit are both $25,000 but are not the same money. Treating them as one pot understates the coverage the law requires.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: $25,000 for one (1) death or injury | $50,000 for two (2) deaths or injuries | $25,000 for property damage

question: What must be carried in your vehicle at all times?
choices: A certificate of insurance or other proof of WV liability insurance, along with a valid vehicle registration card
The original insurance policy document only
A registration card only
Nothing, provided the DMV has your insurance on file electronically
explanation: The handbook pairs the two documents: proof of West Virginia liability insurance and a valid vehicle registration card, carried in the vehicle at all times. Electronic verification by DMV is an enforcement tool, not a substitute for carrying the proof.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance, which can be obtained from your insurance company, must be carried in your vehicle at all times, along with a valid vehicle registration card

question: An officer investigating a crash asks for your proof of insurance, and your paper card is at home. What does the handbook accept?
choices: An image of the certificate displayed on a wireless communication device
A verbal statement of your policy number
Nothing — only the paper certificate is valid
A photograph of your registration card
explanation: The handbook expressly accepts an image displayed on a wireless communication device as valid proof of insurance. You must present the certificate or other proof to any investigating officer after a crash, and at any vehicle inspection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a certificate of insurance or other proof of West Virginia liability insurance, which can be obtained from your insurance company, must be carried in your vehicle at all times, along with a valid vehicle registration card

question: What follows a failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance?
choices: Suspension of both your driver's license and your vehicle registration, plus reinstatement and penalty fees
Suspension of the vehicle registration only
A written warning for a first occurrence
A fine with no effect on the licence
explanation: The handbook says failure to provide proof suspends the driver's license as well as the vehicle registration, along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees. Reinstating either one requires current proof of coverage and payment of the mandatory fees.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance will result in the suspension of your driver's license as well as your vehicle registration along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees.

question: What is the penalty for filing false or fraudulent insurance information?
choices: An additional 90-day licence suspension, revocation of the registration, and possible prosecution carrying up to a $1,000 fine and a year in jail
A $100 fine and three points
A 30-day suspension with no other penalty
Cancellation of the policy by the insurer only
explanation: This is the heaviest penalty in the insurance section: an additional 90-day suspension, revocation of the vehicle registration, and possible prosecution with a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not exceeding one year. Fabricating proof is treated far more seriously than lacking it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Filing of false or fraudulent insurance information will result in an additional 90-day suspension of your driver's license, revocation of your vehicle registration, and possible prosecution that carries a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not to exceed one (1) year.

question: A driver whose policy lapsed shows an officer a screenshot of the cancelled card, altered to show a current date. Beyond driving uninsured, what has he exposed himself to?
choices: An additional 90-day suspension, registration revocation, and prosecution with a fine and possible jail time
Nothing further, since the underlying offense is the same
Three points on his record
A requirement to attend a defensive driving class
explanation: Filing false or fraudulent insurance information is its own offense with its own penalties, stacked on top of the consequences of having no coverage. The handbook's wording — an additional 90-day suspension — shows the penalties are cumulative.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Filing of false or fraudulent insurance information will result in an additional 90-day suspension of your driver's license, revocation of your vehicle registration, and possible prosecution that carries a fine of not more than $1,000 and jail time not to exceed one (1) year.

question: What does West Virginia law say about using an electronic communications device while driving?
choices: It is prohibited on a public street or highway unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment
It is prohibited only for drivers under 18
It is permitted if the vehicle is stopped in traffic
It is permitted for calls but not for text messages
explanation: The prohibition covers any electronic communications device used while driving on a public street or highway, with hands-free equipment as the only general exception. It applies to all drivers, though graduated drivers are held to an even stricter standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: The use of any electronic communications device while driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment.

question: How does the handbook define a hands-free electronic communication device?
choices: One with a feature or function that lets the user engage it without using either or both hands
One that is mounted on the dashboard rather than held
One that switches off automatically when the vehicle moves
One that can be used with a single hand
explanation: The definition turns on engaging the device without the use of either or both hands. That rules out one-handed operation, and mounting a phone does not help if you still have to touch it to use it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: A hands-free electronic communication device has a feature or function that allows the user to engage it without the use of either or both hands.

question: A driver keeps her phone in a dashboard cradle and taps the screen to change a playlist while driving. Does that meet the hands-free standard?
choices: No — hands-free means engaging the device without the use of either or both hands
Yes, because the phone is mounted rather than held
Yes, because changing music is not a communication
Yes, as long as only one hand is used
explanation: The test is whether the device can be engaged without using either or both hands, so tapping a mounted screen fails it. The handbook's list of violations is also broader than conversation, covering data, games, email and text handling.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: A hands-free electronic communication device has a feature or function that allows the user to engage it without the use of either or both hands.

question: Which of these is NOT listed by the handbook as a violation of the device law?
choices: Speaking through a voice-activated hands-free system
Composing a text message on a hand-held phone
Viewing images or data on a hand-held device
Playing a game on a hand-held device
