explanation: Hands-free use is the exception the law creates, so a voice-activated system is what compliance looks like. Everything else listed — composing texts, viewing images or data, playing games — appears in the handbook's own description of the offense.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Violation of this law includes using an electronic communications device that is not enabled as hands-free to engage in a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save, or retrieve an e-mail, text message, or other electronic data.

question: A driver argues she was not on a call, only reading an email at a stop light. How does the handbook treat that?
choices: Reading email on a non-hands-free device is named in the law as a violation
Only calls are covered, so this is lawful
It is lawful because the vehicle was stationary at a light
It is lawful because reading is not transmitting
explanation: The offense expressly includes composing, sending, reading, viewing, accessing, browsing, transmitting, saving or retrieving email, text messages or other electronic data. Nothing in the wording turns on whether the vehicle happens to be stopped in traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Violation of this law includes using an electronic communications device that is not enabled as hands-free to engage in a call, view or transmit images or data, play games, or compose, send, read, view, access, browse, transmit, save, or retrieve an e-mail, text message, or other electronic data.

question: What does a first offense under the hands-free law carry?
choices: A $100 fine and zero points
A $100 fine and two points
A $200 fine and zero points
A $300 fine and three points
explanation: The handbook sets a first offense at a $100 fine and zero points, and a second at $200, also with zero points. Points do not enter the picture until the third offense, which is what makes repeat offending qualitatively different.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: First offense = $100 fine and zero (0) points

question: What does a third or subsequent hands-free violation carry?
choices: A $300 fine and three points
A $300 fine and zero points
A $200 fine and three points
An automatic 90-day suspension
explanation: A third and subsequent offense carries a $300 fine and three points. Because points remain on the record for two years and twelve points makes a licence subject to suspension, the third offense starts moving a driver toward that threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Third and subsequent offenses = $300 and three (3) points

question: A driver receives a third device citation. Beyond the larger fine, what changes compared with the first two?
choices: Points are assessed for the first time — three of them
The licence is revoked immediately
The fine doubles but no points are assessed
The driver must complete a defensive driving class
explanation: The first and second offenses carry zero points; the third and subsequent carry three. Those points behave like any others — they stay two years from conviction and count toward the six-point caution letter and the twelve-point suspension threshold.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Third and subsequent offenses = $300 and three (3) points

question: Which use of a device is expressly not a violation of the law?
choices: Reporting a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the appropriate authorities
Calling a family member to say you will be late
Using a mapping app held in your hand
Reading a work email while stopped in traffic
explanation: The handbook carves out reporting a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard or emergency to the appropriate authorities, and also covers officers, firefighters, EMTs, paramedics and emergency vehicle operators on duty. Ordinary convenience calls are not in the exception.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Use of an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard, or emergency to the appropriate authorities

question: You come upon a tree blocking both lanes on a blind bend and pick up your phone to call it in. How does the handbook treat that?
choices: It is not a violation — reporting a serious road hazard to the authorities is expressly excepted
It is a violation unless the phone is hands-free
It is a violation because you must stop before calling
It is a violation unless you are the first driver on the scene
explanation: Reporting a serious road hazard to the appropriate authorities is one of the named exceptions, alongside fires, crashes and emergencies. A graduated driver at Level 1 or Level 2 should note that their own rule is narrower still, permitting device use only for contacting a 9-1-1 system.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: Use of an electronic communications device to report a fire, traffic crash, serious road hazard, or emergency to the appropriate authorities

question: How long do points remain on a West Virginia driving record?
choices: Two years from the conviction date
One year from the conviction date
Five years from the conviction date
Until the licence is renewed
explanation: Points stay for two years measured from the conviction date, not from the date of the offense or the date you paid. That two-year window is what lets separate incidents combine toward the six- and twelve-point thresholds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points remain on your driving record for two (2) years from the conviction date.

question: A driver was convicted of a point-bearing violation in June 2024 and another in May 2026. How does the handbook's timing rule apply?
choices: Both sets of points are on the record together, because points last two years from conviction
Only the 2026 points count, because each conviction cancels the last
Neither counts, because they are in different years
Only the 2024 points count, because the older conviction is the more serious
explanation: Points from June 2024 remain until June 2026, so a May 2026 conviction lands while they are still live and the totals add together. This overlap is exactly how drivers reach the six-point caution letter without any single serious offense.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points remain on your driving record for two (2) years from the conviction date.

question: What does the DMV do when a driver reaches six points or more?
choices: Sends a letter of caution urging care and obedience to traffic laws
Suspends the licence for 30 days
Requires a defensive driving class
Orders a re-examination
explanation: Six points or more triggers a letter of caution — a warning rather than a sanction. The consequence with teeth arrives at twelve points, where the licence becomes subject to suspension.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you have six (6) points or more on your record, the DMV will send you a letter of caution, urging you to be careful while driving and obedient of traffic laws.

question: What happens at 12 points?
choices: The driver's license is subject to suspension
The driver receives a second letter of caution
Three points are automatically removed
The licence is permanently revoked
explanation: Twelve points makes the licence subject to suspension. Revocation is reserved for the specific serious convictions the handbook lists separately, so accumulating points leads to suspension rather than permanent loss.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you accumulate 12 points on your record, your driver's license is subject to suspension.

question: Which pairing of point total and consequence is correct?
choices: 12 points — the licence is subject to suspension
6 points — the licence is subject to suspension
12 points — a letter of caution is sent
3 points — the licence is subject to suspension
explanation: Six points brings the letter of caution and twelve makes the licence subject to suspension. Three is the number of points an approved defensive driving class removes, which is a different use of the same figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you accumulate 12 points on your record, your driver's license is subject to suspension.

question: How can a driver have points removed from their record?
choices: By completing an approved eight-hour defensive driving class, which deducts three points once every 12 months
By completing any defensive driving class, as often as they like
By going 12 months without a conviction, which clears the record
By paying a reinstatement fee to the DMV
explanation: An approved eight-hour defensive driving class deducts three points, and a motorist is only eligible for that reduction once every 12 months. It is the only point-removal route the handbook offers, apart from points simply ageing off after two years.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may have three (3) points deducted from your record by completing an approved eight (8) hour defensive driving class.  Motorists are only eligible for this point reduction once every 12 months.

question: A driver enrolls in a defensive driving class the day after conviction, before the points appear on the record. What is the effect?
choices: No deduction — the class must not be taken before the points appear on the record
Three points are deducted as soon as the points post
Six points are deducted for acting promptly
The conviction is removed from the record entirely
explanation: The handbook rules out a deduction for a class taken before the points appear on your record, and equally for a class the DMV has not approved. Timing and approval are both conditions, so being quick can actually cost the driver the benefit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you take a class without approval from the DMV or take the class prior to the points appearing on your record, you will not be eligible for the point deduction.

question: Which of these would NOT disqualify a driver from the three-point deduction?
choices: Taking the approved class after the points have appeared on the record
Taking a class the DMV has not approved
Taking the class before the points appear on the record
Having already used the reduction six months ago
explanation: Taking an approved class after the points have posted is exactly what qualifies. The other three each fall foul of a stated condition: approval, timing, or the once-every-12-months limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you take a class without approval from the DMV or take the class prior to the points appearing on your record, you will not be eligible for the point deduction.

question: How are point values assigned to violations?
choices: According to the seriousness of the in-state or out-of-state moving violation
Equally, at two points for every moving violation
By the amount of the fine imposed by the court
Only for violations committed inside West Virginia
explanation: Points are assigned to in-state and out-of-state moving violations depending on the seriousness of the violation, so more dangerous conduct carries more points. Out-of-state violations reach your record through the Driver License Compact.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations depending on the seriousness of the violation.

question: A driver assumes a ticket from a neighbouring state cannot affect their West Virginia point total. Why is that wrong?
choices: Points are assigned to out-of-state as well as in-state moving violations
Only violations resulting in a crash are recorded
Out-of-state tickets add double points
Out-of-state tickets affect insurance but never the DMV record
explanation: The handbook says points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations. West Virginia's membership of the Driver License Compact is what brings those out-of-state convictions onto the record in the first place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Points have been assigned to various in-state and out-of-state moving traffic violations depending on the seriousness of the violation.

question: Which conviction involving a graduated driver requires revocation of the licence?
choices: Two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
One moving violation conviction as a graduated driver
Any conviction for a parking violation
Three moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
explanation: The mandatory revocation list includes two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver. This is the same threshold that ends the GDL road in Chapter I, stated here as a revocation the DMV must impose on notice of final conviction.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Two (2) or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver

question: A Level 2 driver is convicted of a second moving violation. Which part of the handbook, besides the GDL rules, applies?
choices: The mandatory revocation list, which includes two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver
The point system's six-point letter of caution provision
The compulsory insurance verification programme
The re-examination provisions for unsafe drivers
explanation: The same facts appear in two places: Chapter I ends the graduated driver's privilege until 18, and Chapter II lists two or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver among the convictions requiring immediate revocation. Nothing about it is discretionary once the conviction is final.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Two (2) or more moving violation convictions as a graduated driver

question: Which of these is on the handbook's mandatory revocation list?
choices: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury
Receiving a second parking ticket in a year
Failing to carry proof of insurance on one occasion
Accumulating six points on your record
explanation: Leaving the scene of a crash resulting in death or personal injury is named on the list of convictions requiring immediate revocation. Six points brings only a caution letter, and an insurance proof failure leads to suspension rather than mandatory revocation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury

question: Which statement about leaving the scene of an injury crash is NOT correct?
choices: It results in points but leaves the licence intact
It appears on the list of convictions requiring immediate revocation
The DMV must revoke on notice of final conviction
It is treated more seriously than an ordinary moving violation
explanation: This offense is not handled through points at all — it sits on the mandatory revocation list, where the DMV must revoke on receiving notice of final conviction. Treating it as a points matter understates it substantially.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Leaving the scene of a crash that results in death or personal injury

question: What may follow driving while your licence is suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason?
choices: A 90-day suspension
A warning letter
Three points and a $100 fine
Immediate reinstatement once the fine is paid
explanation: The handbook describes driving while suspended or revoked for a non-DUI reason as a serious matter that may cause a 90-day suspension. Driving while revoked on a DUI is treated separately and far more severely, including mandatory jail time.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Driving While a Driver's License Is Revoked or Suspended
source.sourceQuote: Driving while your driver's license is suspended or revoked (non-DUI related) is a serious matter and may cause a 90-day suspension.

question: A driver under a 30-day suspension drives to work and is stopped. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: A further 90-day suspension may follow, because driving while suspended is a serious matter
Nothing further, because the original suspension already covers it
The original suspension is converted to a revocation for life
The driver receives points but no additional suspension
explanation: Driving while suspended is a separate offense that may cause a 90-day suspension on top of what the driver is already serving. Needing to get to work is not an exception the handbook recognises — a restricted licence, where available, is granted by DMV rather than assumed by the driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Driving While a Driver's License Is Revoked or Suspended
source.sourceQuote: Driving while your driver's license is suspended or revoked (non-DUI related) is a serious matter and may cause a 90-day suspension.

question: What penalty does the handbook attach to using someone else's licence as your own?
choices: A 90-day suspension
A $100 fine and no suspension
A 30-day suspension
Permanent revocation
explanation: The 90-day suspension covers a family of offenses: using another person's licence, letting someone use yours, letting someone use your identity documents to obtain a licence, and using or displaying a fictitious licence. Lending your card is penalised the same way as borrowing one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is also illegal to use someone else's license as your own, to permit someone else to use your driver's license, to permit someone to use your identity documents to obtain a license, or to use or display a fictitious license.  The penalty for these offenses is a 90-day suspension.

question: A 17-year-old lends his licence to a friend who has none. Who faces the 90-day suspension?
choices: Both — permitting someone else to use your licence is itself a listed offense
Only the friend who used it
Only the owner, if the friend is caught driving
Neither, unless the friend is involved in a crash
explanation: The handbook lists using someone else's licence and permitting someone else to use yours as separate offenses, each carrying a 90-day suspension. The owner is not a bystander in this arrangement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: It is also illegal to use someone else's license as your own, to permit someone else to use your driver's license, to permit someone to use your identity documents to obtain a license, or to use or display a fictitious license.  The penalty for these offenses is a 90-day suspension.

question: What happens if you fail to appear or comply with a ticket or court order?
choices: The DMV suspends your licence until you show proof of compliance and pay all penalty fees
The court issues a warning and takes no DMV action
Points are added but the licence is unaffected
The DMV suspends the licence for a fixed 30 days
explanation: Courts are required to notify the DMV of a failure to appear or comply with any ticket, court order or decision, even a non-traffic one, and the DMV suspends until you present proof of compliance and pay the fees. The suspension has no fixed end date — it ends when you resolve the underlying matter.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Failure to Comply with In-State Citations
source.sourceQuote: The DMV will suspend your driver's license until you present proof of compliance with the court action and all penalty fees are paid.

question: Which statement about failing to comply with a court action is NOT correct?
choices: Only traffic tickets can lead to a DMV suspension
Municipal, magistrate and circuit courts must notify the DMV
The suspension lasts until proof of compliance is presented
All penalty fees must be paid before reinstatement
explanation: The handbook says courts must notify the DMV of a failure to appear or comply with any type of ticket, court order or decision, even if it is not a traffic ticket. That is the detail drivers most often get wrong about this rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Failure to Comply with In-State Citations
source.sourceQuote: The DMV will suspend your driver's license until you present proof of compliance with the court action and all penalty fees are paid.

question: What does West Virginia's membership of the Driver License Compact mean for violations committed in other states?
choices: They become part of your West Virginia driving record and points may be assessed
They remain with the state that issued them and never reach WV
They are recorded but can never carry points
They apply only if the other state is adjacent to West Virginia
explanation: Under the compact, traffic violations received in other states join your West Virginia record and, if warranted, points are assessed. A conviction elsewhere that is grounds for suspension or revocation can also cost you the WV licence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia is a member of the Driver License Compact.  Traffic violations you receive in other states will become part of your West Virginia driving record and, if warranted, points will be assessed.

question: A WV driver is convicted of speeding while on holiday in another compact state and assumes it stays there. What actually happens?
choices: The violation becomes part of their WV driving record and points may be assessed
Nothing, because WV only records violations committed in WV
The WV licence is automatically suspended for 30 days
The driver must surrender their WV licence to that state
explanation: The compact exists precisely to stop violations being confined to the state where they happened, so the conviction joins the WV record and can draw points. If the offense is grounds for suspension or revocation, the WV licence itself may be suspended or revoked.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: West Virginia is a member of the Driver License Compact.  Traffic violations you receive in other states will become part of your West Virginia driving record and, if warranted, points will be assessed.

question: A driver receives a DMV notice asking for proof of coverage and ignores it. What does the handbook say follows?
choices: Suspension of the driver's license and the vehicle registration, with reinstatement and penalty fees to follow
A warning letter, with action only if a second notice is ignored
Suspension of the registration, leaving the licence untouched
Nothing, because DMV verifies coverage electronically without the driver's help
explanation: The DMV may verify insurance at any point in the registration year and will require proof when it issues a notice. Failing to provide that proof suspends the licence as well as the registration, and reinstating either requires current proof of coverage plus the mandatory fees.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Failure to provide proof of West Virginia liability insurance will result in the suspension of your driver's license as well as your vehicle registration along with reinstatement and/or penalty fees.

question: Which statement about the hands-free law is NOT correct?
choices: It applies only while the vehicle is in motion on an interstate
It covers any electronic communications device
It applies on public streets and highways
Hands-free equipment is the general exception
explanation: The law is written for driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway, not for interstates alone, and the handbook's list of covered conduct extends well beyond a moving vehicle on a freeway. Device type, road type and the hands-free exception are all stated as described in the other three options.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: The use of any electronic communications device while driving a motor vehicle on a public street or highway is prohibited unless the use is accomplished by hands-free equipment.

question: Which pairing of hands-free offense and penalty is correct?
choices: First offense — $100 fine and zero points
First offense — $100 fine and three points
Second offense — $300 fine and three points
First offense — $300 fine and zero points
explanation: The escalation runs $100 with no points, then $200 with no points, then $300 with three points from the third offense onward. Points arrive only at the third stage, so pairing them with a first offense misstates the scheme.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: The Use of Communication Devices While Operating a Motor Vehicle
source.sourceQuote: First offense = $100 fine and zero (0) points

question: A driver reaches seven points and receives DMV correspondence. What is it most likely to be, and what does it mean?
choices: A letter of caution, which urges care and obedience to traffic laws but does not itself suspend anything
A suspension notice, because any total above six suspends the licence
A notice requiring an eight-hour defensive driving class
A notice of mandatory revocation
explanation: Six points or more triggers a letter of caution urging the driver to be careful and obedient to traffic laws. Suspension does not become a prospect until twelve points, so the letter is a warning that there is real headroom left to lose.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you have six (6) points or more on your record, the DMV will send you a letter of caution, urging you to be careful while driving and obedient of traffic laws.

question: Which statement about the defensive driving point reduction is NOT correct?
choices: A driver may use the reduction as often as they accumulate points
It removes three points
The class must be an approved eight-hour class
A driver is eligible only once every 12 months
explanation: The handbook limits the reduction to once every 12 months, so it cannot be used repeatedly to offset a run of convictions. The three-point value, the eight-hour approved class and the annual eligibility limit are all stated as given.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You may have three (3) points deducted from your record by completing an approved eight (8) hour defensive driving class.  Motorists are only eligible for this point reduction once every 12 months.

question: Who has to pass the vision screening?
choices: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals
New applicants only
Drivers over the age of 65 only
Applicants who do not already wear glasses
explanation: The handbook applies the screening to all persons, new applicants and renewals alike. Vision can change between renewals, which is why an existing licence does not exempt anyone.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals, will have to pass the vision screening.

question: A driver renewing a licence held for 20 years asks whether the eye test still applies. What is the answer?
choices: Yes — all persons, new applicants and renewals, must pass the vision screening
No — screening applies only to first-time applicants
Only if the current licence carries a corrective lenses restriction
Only if the driver has points on their record
explanation: Renewals are named alongside new applicants in the screening requirement. Neither length of driving history nor an existing restriction changes it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: All persons, whether new applicants or renewals, will have to pass the vision screening.

question: What vision standard passes the screening?
choices: 20/40 or better using both eyes, with or without conventional corrective lenses, and no serious visual defect
20/20 or better using both eyes, without corrective lenses
20/60 or better using both eyes, with corrective lenses
20/40 or better in the right eye only
explanation: The standard is 20/40 or better using both eyes, reached with or without conventional corrective lenses, and with no serious visual defect. Glasses and contacts are allowed to get you there — what matters is the corrected result.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is 20/40 or better using both eyes, either with or without conventional corrective lenses, and you show no serious visual defect, you will pass the vision screening.

question: Which applicant would pass the vision screening as the handbook describes it?
choices: One reading 20/35 with both eyes while wearing prescribed contact lenses, with no serious visual defect
One reading 20/50 with both eyes while wearing prescribed glasses
One reaching 20/40 only with the aid of a telescopic lens arrangement
One reading 20/40 but with a serious visual defect
explanation: Reaching 20/40 or better with conventional corrective lenses passes, so 20/35 with contacts is fine. Twenty over fifty falls short, a serious visual defect fails regardless of acuity, and the handbook says special arrangements such as bi-optic or telescopic lenses may not be used to satisfy the standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is 20/40 or better using both eyes, either with or without conventional corrective lenses, and you show no serious visual defect, you will pass the vision screening.

question: What appears on the licence of someone who needs glasses to reach 20/40?
choices: A restriction code for corrective lenses
A note in the DMV file, but nothing on the card
An endorsement allowing daytime driving only
A vertical card format
explanation: Needing glasses or contacts to reach 20/40 puts a corrective lenses restriction code on the licence. Restriction codes appear in the restrictions field on the front of the card and are explained on the back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you require glasses or contact lenses to have a vision level of 20/40 or better, your driver's license will show a restriction code for “corrective lenses.”

question: A driver whose licence carries the corrective lenses restriction arrives for a road test without their glasses. What is the consequence?
choices: Failing to wear glasses when required is listed among the road skills test automatic failures
The test proceeds, with points deducted for the omission
The examiner may lend the applicant reading glasses
Nothing, provided the applicant can read the test route signs
explanation: The handbook lists failing to wear your glasses if required among the errors that disqualify you from the road test. Away from the test it is just as serious, because driving in violation of a restriction can suspend or revoke the privilege.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you require glasses or contact lenses to have a vision level of 20/40 or better, your driver's license will show a restriction code for “corrective lenses.”

question: Can an applicant with sight in only one eye pass the vision screening?
choices: Yes, if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better
No, both eyes are always required
Yes, but only with a daylight driving restriction
Yes, if the vision level with that eye is 20/60 or better
explanation: The handbook says an applicant with only one eye may be passed if that eye reaches 20/40 or better. The acuity standard does not change — what changes is that it is measured in the one eye available.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you have only one (1) eye, you may be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better.

question: A driver who lost the sight of one eye years ago is renewing a licence and reads 20/30 with the remaining eye. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: They may be passed, because the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better
They cannot be passed, because both eyes are required
They may be passed only with a daylight driving restriction
They must first obtain a statement from the Driver's License Advisory Board
explanation: The handbook allows an applicant with only one eye to be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better, and 20/30 clears that. The specialist statement route exists for applicants who cannot reach 20/40, which is not this driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you have only one (1) eye, you may be passed if the vision level with that eye is 20/40 or better.

question: What happens to an applicant whose vision is less than 20/40?
choices: They do not pass, and are advised to consult a vision specialist about reaching the 20/40 level
They are issued a licence restricted to daylight driving
They may retake the screening the same day
They are permanently barred from holding a licence
explanation: Falling short means not passing the screening and being advised to see a vision specialist to determine whether the vision can be brought to 20/40. A specialist's DLAB-Form 2 statement can bring the application forward again, possibly with restrictions, so it is not a permanent bar.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is less than 20/40 or you have a serious visual defect, you will not pass the screening and will be advised to consult a vision specialist to determine if your vision can be brought to the 20/40 level.

question: Which statement about failing the vision screening is NOT correct?
choices: The applicant is permanently ineligible for a West Virginia licence
The applicant will not pass the screening
The applicant is advised to consult a vision specialist
The question is whether the vision can be brought to the 20/40 level
explanation: Nothing in the handbook makes a failed screening permanent — it routes the applicant to a vision specialist, whose statement on a DLAB-Form 2 may be reviewed by the Driver's License Advisory Board. The other three statements track the passage exactly.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vision is less than 20/40 or you have a serious visual defect, you will not pass the screening and will be advised to consult a vision specialist to determine if your vision can be brought to the 20/40 level.

question: How many questions does the knowledge examination have, and where do they come from?
choices: At least 25, based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings found in the handbook
Exactly 40, drawn from West Virginia state code
At least 25, drawn from national driving standards
Exactly 20, covering signs and markings only
explanation: The examination has at least 25 questions and every topic it draws on is in this handbook: basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings. That is the strongest argument for studying the handbook itself rather than anything else.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The knowledge examination has at least 25 questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs, and markings found in the  handbook.

question: Which subject areas does the handbook say the knowledge examination covers?
choices: Basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings
Vehicle mechanics and maintenance schedules
State code citations and court procedure
Insurance products and premium calculations
explanation: The five named areas are basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs and markings. Everything the test asks about is meant to be findable in the handbook, which is why unfamiliar material is a sign you are studying the wrong source.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The knowledge examination has at least 25 questions based on the basic knowledge, traffic rules, regulations, signs, and markings found in the  handbook.

question: How many of the 25 questions must you answer correctly to pass?
explanation: The pass mark is 19 out of 25, which leaves room for six wrong answers and no more. Any practice target above that, such as aiming for 22, is preparation margin rather than the official standard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must answer 19 out of the 25 questions correctly to pass the test.

question: An applicant answers 25 questions and gets 6 wrong. What is the result?
choices: A pass, because 19 correct answers meets the standard
A fail, because more than five wrong answers is disqualifying
A fail, because 20 correct answers are required
A pass, but only with a retest of the missed questions
explanation: Nineteen correct out of 25 is exactly the pass mark, and six wrong leaves precisely 19 right. One more error would fail the test, which is why the margin at 19 is worth treating as no margin at all.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You must answer 19 out of the 25 questions correctly to pass the test.

question: What happens to questions you have not answered when the time limit expires?
choices: They are considered incorrect
They are not counted either way
The test is extended until they are answered
They are marked correct if the rest of the test is passed
explanation: The handbook states that any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect. A blank therefore costs the same as a wrong answer, which is why leaving questions to come back to is a risk.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: There is a time limit on the test and any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect.

question: You are unsure of three questions with little time left. What does the handbook's rule suggest you do?
choices: Answer all of them before time expires, since unanswered questions count as incorrect
Leave them blank, since blanks are not counted
Ask the examiner to pause the clock while you think
Answer only the ones you are confident about
explanation: Because unanswered questions are treated as incorrect, an uncertain answer can only help while a blank certainly cannot. There is nothing in the handbook allowing the clock to be paused, and DMV staff may not help explain questions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: There is a time limit on the test and any questions not answered in the prescribed time will be considered incorrect.

question: What accommodation does the handbook describe for the reading impaired?
choices: Audio versions of the knowledge examination, administered with headphones
Unlimited time to complete the printed exam
A DMV employee who reads each question aloud
A reduced set of 15 questions
explanation: Audio versions are available for the reading impaired and are administered with headphones. Headsets are limited, so the handbook warns you may have to wait if you request the audio test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Audio versions of the knowledge examination are available for the reading impaired.  The test is administered with headphones.

question: What may a DMV employee do to help an applicant during the knowledge examination?
choices: Nothing beyond what a printed-exam applicant would receive — they may not read, re-word or explain questions
Read each question aloud on request
Re-word confusing questions in simpler language
Explain the meaning of any term the applicant does not know
explanation: The handbook bars DMV employees from reading the test to you, re-wording information, or providing extra help explaining questions that a printed-exam applicant would not get. The audio version exists precisely so the accommodation is standardised rather than left to staff.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Employees of the DMV are not to read the test to you, re-word the information, or provide additional help explaining questions that would not be supplied to applicants taking the printed knowledge exam.

question: Which statement about the audio version of the knowledge examination is NOT correct?
choices: An examiner may explain any question the applicant finds unclear
The same information covered in the printed exam is covered in the audio version
The same rules apply to the audio version
Headsets are limited and an applicant may have to wait
explanation: Explanation is exactly what the handbook rules out — employees may not read the test, re-word it or explain questions beyond what printed-exam applicants receive. Equal content, equal rules and limited headsets are all stated.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Employees of the DMV are not to read the test to you, re-word the information, or provide additional help explaining questions that would not be supplied to applicants taking the printed knowledge exam.

question: An applicant who reads with difficulty asks how to take the test. What does the handbook offer?
choices: An audio version administered with headphones, covering the same information under the same rules
A shorter version with fewer questions
An oral examination conducted by a DMV employee
An exemption from the knowledge test with a doctor's letter
explanation: The audio version is the accommodation the handbook provides, delivered by headphones, covering the same information and governed by the same rules. It is specifically not a staff member reading the test, which employees are forbidden to do.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Audio versions of the knowledge examination are available for the reading impaired.  The test is administered with headphones.

question: What must the testing vehicle have before it can be used for the road skills test?
choices: A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance
A valid inspection sticker only
Proof of insurance and a spare tire
Nothing specific, as long as it runs
explanation: A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle are both required before it can be used, and the examiner checks compliance with registration, inspection and equipment laws. Defects in the vehicle may constitute failure of the examination.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The testing vehicle must first be checked to make sure it complies with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws.  A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle is required before the vehicle can be used for the road skills test.

question: You arrive for your road test in a car whose inspection sticker expired last month. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: The vehicle cannot be used for the road skills test, because a valid inspection sticker is required
The test proceeds with a warning to renew the inspection
The examiner may issue a temporary inspection waiver
The test proceeds if proof of insurance is produced
explanation: A valid inspection sticker is a precondition for using the vehicle, standing alongside proof of insurance rather than as an alternative to it. Vehicle defects and non-compliance may constitute failure of the examination.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The testing vehicle must first be checked to make sure it complies with registration, vehicle inspection and equipment laws.  A valid inspection sticker and proof of insurance on the vehicle is required before the vehicle can be used for the road skills test.

question: A defect is found in your test vehicle. What does the handbook allow?
choices: The examiner may permit a minor defect to be corrected and the examination continued, but not in another vehicle the same day
You may fetch a different vehicle and continue immediately
The examination continues regardless, with points deducted
You must return in seven days regardless of the defect
explanation: The examiner may allow a minor defect to be corrected so the examination can continue, but the handbook is explicit that you will not be permitted to continue in another vehicle on the same test date. Switching cars is the option that is closed off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you will not be permitted to continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date

question: Your test is stopped because of a vehicle defect and your friend offers to lend you her car, parked nearby. Why does that not solve the problem?
choices: You may not continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date
Her car would also need a road test of its own
Only a vehicle owned by the applicant may be used
The examiner would need written permission from the owner
explanation: The rule closes the same-day switch: you cannot continue the examination in another vehicle on that test date. Bringing a compliant vehicle in the first place is the only way around it, since the vehicle check happens before you drive.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: you will not be permitted to continue the examination in another vehicle on the same test date

question: What does the handbook require you to know about the vehicle's safety equipment?
choices: Its location and function, including the parking/emergency brake — being unable to locate and demonstrate any of it is an automatic failure
Only the location of the seat belts and mirrors
Only how to operate the headlights and wipers
Nothing, as the examiner points each item out
explanation: You must know the location and function of all safety equipment, the parking/emergency brake included, and being unable to both locate and demonstrate any of it is an automatic failure on the road skills test. Knowing where it is without being able to use it is not enough.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The applicant must know the location and function of all safety equipment, including the parking/emergency brake.  If the applicant is unable to both locate and demonstrate the use of any of the vehicle safety equipment, this will result in an automatic failure on the road skills test.

question: Which statement about vehicle safety equipment on test day is NOT correct?
choices: Knowing where an item is located is sufficient, even if you cannot operate it
You must know the location and function of all safety equipment
The parking/emergency brake is specifically named
Being unable to locate and demonstrate any item is an automatic failure
explanation: The handbook requires you to both locate and demonstrate the use of the equipment, so pointing at a control you cannot work does not satisfy it. That is why practising in the exact vehicle you will test in matters.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The applicant must know the location and function of all safety equipment, including the parking/emergency brake.  If the applicant is unable to both locate and demonstrate the use of any of the vehicle safety equipment, this will result in an automatic failure on the road skills test.

question: At what point does window tint become illegal equipment?
choices: When windows are tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission
When windows are tinted at all
When windows are tinted to less than 70 percent light transmission
Only when the windshield itself is tinted
explanation: The illegal equipment list names windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission. Because tint is checked as part of the vehicle check, it can stop a road test before it starts.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission

question: You have aftermarket tint on your side windows and plan to use the car for your road test. Why is that worth checking first?
choices: Tint below 35 percent light transmission is illegal equipment, and vehicle defects may constitute failure of examination
Tint is only an issue for night-time road tests
Tint is permitted on side windows but not the rear window
Tint has no bearing on the road test
explanation: Window tint under 35 percent light transmission appears on the illegal equipment list, and the examiner checks the vehicle against the equipment laws before the test. The handbook also says the examiner cannot give the driving test unless the vehicle is legally equipped.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Windows tinted to less than 35 percent light transmission

question: Why are red and/or blue flashing lights on the illegal equipment list?
choices: Only authorized emergency vehicles may have those warning lights
They draw too much power from the vehicle's battery
They are permitted only on vehicles over a certain weight
They are legal but must be covered when not in use
explanation: The handbook explains the entry itself: only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights. Sirens, bells and whistles are listed alongside them for the same reason — they imitate an emergency vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Red and/or blue flashing lights (Only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights)

question: Which of these is NOT on the handbook's illegal equipment list?
choices: A single working spotlight
Sirens, bells, or whistles
A cutout or loud-sounding muffler
A broken or cracked windshield
explanation: The list bars more than one spotlight, so a single spotlight is not itself prohibited. Sirens and bells, loud mufflers and a broken or cracked windshield are all named, and any of them can stop the road test at the vehicle check.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Red and/or blue flashing lights (Only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights)

question: When is the road test given?
choices: Only after you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination
On the same visit as the knowledge test, before it is marked
Before the knowledge examination, to save a second trip
Only after a second vision screening
explanation: The road test is not given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination. That ordering, plus the minimum permit-holding period from Chapter I, sets how quickly anyone can reach a licence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The road test, or driving examination, will not be given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination.

question: An applicant asks to take the road test first because they are a confident driver but a nervous test-taker. What does the handbook allow?
choices: Nothing — the road test is not given until the knowledge examination has been passed
The order may be reversed at the examiner's discretion
Both may be taken on the same day in either order
The knowledge test may be waived for an experienced driver
explanation: The sequence is fixed: the road test follows the knowledge examination. Confidence behind the wheel does not substitute for the knowledge the written test measures, which is drawn entirely from this handbook.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The road test, or driving examination, will not be given until you have passed all other parts of the knowledge examination.

question: What does the handbook tell you to do before driving away on the test?
choices: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror, because proper seat adjustment assures better control
Test the horn and the hazard lights
Drive a lap of the car park to warm up
Ask the examiner to confirm the route in advance
explanation: Adjusting the seat and rear view mirror before driving is stated directly, and the handbook explains why: proper seat adjustment assures better control of the vehicle, and a correct mirror helps you see behind when slowing, changing lanes or turning.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror before driving.  Proper seat  adjustment assures better control of the vehicle.

question: Which habit does the handbook specifically warn against during the driving examination?
choices: Resting your elbow in the window instead of keeping both hands on the wheel
Checking your mirrors too frequently
Signalling earlier than necessary
Braking gently on approach to a stop
explanation: The handbook says to keep both hands on the steering wheel and not to rest your elbow in the window. Elsewhere it adds that all steering methods are acceptable provided both hands stay on the outside of the wheel, with no palming.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Adjust the vehicle seat and rear view mirror before driving.  Proper seat  adjustment assures better control of the vehicle.

question: Which exercises may form part of the basic control skills test?
choices: Left and right side parallel parking, forward and reverse two-point turnabouts, and a three-point turnabout
Hill starts, emergency braking and skid recovery
Highway merging and lane changes at speed
Reversing around a corner and an emergency stop only
explanation: The handbook lists five exercises and says you may be tested on a subset of them: left side parallel park, right side parallel park, forward two-point turnabout, reverse two-point turnabout, and three-point turnabout. It also advises practising them with a licensed adult over 21 in a safe place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: During the test, you may be tested on a subset of the following Basic Control Skills exercises:

question: How should you prepare for the basic control skills exercises, according to the handbook?
choices: Practise them with a properly licensed person over 21 in a safe place until you can complete them correctly
Practise them alone on quiet public roads at night
Wait for the examiner to demonstrate each one on test day
Practise only parallel parking, since the others are optional
explanation: The handbook recommends practising with a parent, guardian or friend who is properly licensed and over 21, in a safe place such as a parking lot or residential area, and in a variety of vehicles and locations. You may be tested on any subset of the exercises, so none of them is safe to skip.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: During the test, you may be tested on a subset of the following Basic Control Skills exercises:

question: How are turn signal mistakes scored during the exercises?
choices: Each failure to use or improper use of the signal counts as an error
Only the first missed signal is counted
Signal errors are noted but do not affect the score
Signal errors count only during lane changes
explanation: Every instance counts: each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it is an error. The handbook adds that if your signal cancels automatically you must reactivate it when necessary, so a cancelled signal mid-manoeuvre is your responsibility.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: Each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it will count as an error.

question: During an exercise your signal cancels itself partway through the manoeuvre and you do not switch it back on. How is that treated?
choices: As an error, because a signal that cancels automatically must be reactivated when necessary
As acceptable, because the signal was used at the start
As acceptable, because automatic cancellation is a vehicle function
As an automatic failure of the road test
explanation: The handbook expressly puts the burden on the driver to reactivate a signal that cancels automatically. It counts as a signal error rather than an automatic failure — but signal errors accumulate, and excessive points during the road test is itself disqualifying.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: How To Prepare For Your Driver's Test
source.sourceQuote: Each time you fail to use or improperly use your turn signal it will count as an error.

question: How far back should you stop behind another vehicle?
choices: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
One full car length, measured by eye
Close enough that your bumper nearly touches theirs
Three car lengths in all conditions
explanation: The handbook gives a practical reference rather than a distance: stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead. It works at any vehicle height and leaves room to pull around if the car in front cannot move.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A safe gap when stopping behind another vehicle is to stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

question: You stop behind a car at a red light and can see only the top of its rear bumper. What does the handbook's reference tell you?
choices: You are too close — you should be able to see the vehicle's rear tires
You are correctly positioned for a traffic light
You are too far back and should close the gap
The reference applies only at stop signs
explanation: Being unable to see the rear tires means the gap is smaller than the handbook's safe-gap reference. The same guidance appears for stopping behind a vehicle at intersections and before turns, so it is not limited to one kind of stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: A safe gap when stopping behind another vehicle is to stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

question: What should you expect regarding traffic signs during the road test?
choices: To be asked to identify a number of signs, which can be located anywhere on the route
To be shown printed sign cards at the end of the test
To be asked about signs only if you make a driving error
Nothing — signs are covered only in the knowledge test
explanation: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs, and they can be anywhere on the route. The handbook adds that if the examiner asks what sign you just passed, you should be able to tell them — which means noticing signs as you drive, not just recognising them on a card.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs.  They can be located anywhere on the road test.

question: The examiner asks what the sign you just passed meant, and you did not notice it. What does this tell you about how to drive the test?
choices: Signs must be actively read as you drive, because you may be asked about any sign on the route
Only signs at intersections are examinable
The examiner will always point out a sign before asking about it
Sign questions are optional and can be declined
explanation: The handbook says the signs can be located anywhere on the road test and that you should be able to tell the examiner about a sign you just passed. That is a scan-and-read habit, not a memorisation exercise, and it is the same habit that keeps a licensed driver safe.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: During the road test you will be asked to identify a number of traffic signs.  They can be located anywhere on the road test.

question: Which of these is listed as an automatic failure?
choices: Hitting, tapping or moving a cone, barrel or flag
Stalling the engine once during the test
Signalling later than the examiner expected
Braking more firmly than necessary at a stop sign
explanation: The automatic failures list names hitting, tapping or moving a cone, barrel or flag, along with jumping a curb and accumulating excessive points. Touching a marker at all is enough — the handbook does not distinguish between a tap and a knock.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Hitting, tapping, or moving a cone, barrel, or flag

question: During a parallel parking exercise your rear tire brushes a cone, which rocks but does not fall. What is the result?
choices: An automatic failure — hitting, tapping or moving a cone is disqualifying
An error scored as points, not a failure
No penalty, since the cone stayed upright
A warning, with the exercise repeated
explanation: The handbook covers hitting, tapping or moving the marker, so a cone that rocks has been moved. Jumping a curb during any part of the driving test is treated the same way, which is why slow, deliberate positioning beats speed in these exercises.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Hitting, tapping, or moving a cone, barrel, or flag

question: What happens if you do not use your safety belt during the road test?
choices: You are disqualified
You lose points but may continue
You are warned once and then disqualified
Nothing, if the examiner is belted
explanation: Not using your safety belt appears on the list of errors that disqualify you from the road test. The road test score form carries it as a separate automatic failure line, so it is checked deliberately rather than incidentally.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you do not use your safety belt

question: Which of these road-test errors is NOT an automatic disqualification?
choices: Stopping slightly further back from the stop line than necessary
Not using your safety belt
Using a wireless communications device at any time
Failing to yield to pedestrians or other roadway users
explanation: Stopping a little early is a positioning matter scored as points, whereas belts, devices and failing to yield are all named among the road skills test automatic failures. Knowing which errors are recoverable helps you keep composure when one happens.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you do not use your safety belt

question: When may you use a wireless communications device during the road test?
choices: Never — using it at any time disqualifies you
Only to answer a call from a parent or guardian
Only when the vehicle is stopped
Only hands-free, as with ordinary driving
explanation: The handbook uses the words 'if at anytime you use your wireless communications device' among the disqualifying errors, leaving no exception for hands-free use or for a stopped vehicle. The safest approach is to leave the phone switched off and out of reach.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If at anytime you use your wireless communications device

question: Your phone rings during the road test and you decline the call with one tap. What is the result?
choices: Disqualification — using the device at any time during the test ends it
Nothing, because you did not answer the call
A points deduction for distraction
Nothing, provided the examiner did not have to intervene
explanation: Declining a call is still using the device, and the disqualification is written to cover any use at any time. Because this is one of the easiest automatic failures to avoid entirely, the phone belongs switched off before the test begins.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If at anytime you use your wireless communications device

question: What does the handbook say if the examiner has to take control of the vehicle?
choices: You are disqualified
The test is paused and resumed
Points are deducted for the incident
The manoeuvre is repeated
explanation: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle you are disqualified. The same list also disqualifies you for committing an unsafe act or forcing another driver to take evasive action, so the standard is about danger created, not just the intervention itself.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle

question: Which situation matches the handbook's automatic failure for examiner intervention?
choices: The examiner grabs the wheel as you drift toward an oncoming vehicle
The examiner repeats a direction you did not hear
The examiner points out a sign you missed
The examiner asks you to pull over at the end of the route
explanation: Taking control of the vehicle means physically intervening in the driving, as with grabbing the wheel or the brake. Repeating a direction or asking a question is normal examiner communication, not intervention.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the examiner has to take control of the vehicle

question: A licence requires corrective lenses and the applicant arrives without them. How does the road test treat this?
choices: Failing to wear your glasses if required is a disqualifying error
The test proceeds with a points deduction
The test proceeds if the applicant can read a sign at 20 metres
The applicant is rescheduled without penalty
explanation: The road skills test automatic failures include failing to wear your glasses if required. This connects directly to the vision screening, where needing lenses to reach 20/40 is what puts the restriction on the licence in the first place.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you fail to wear your glasses if required

question: Which statement about required glasses is NOT correct?
choices: An applicant may substitute sunglasses if prescription lenses are forgotten
Failing to wear required glasses disqualifies you on the road test
The requirement arises from the vision screening result
The restriction is recorded as a code on the licence
explanation: Nothing in the handbook permits substituting a different pair of lenses for the prescription the restriction requires. The other statements describe the chain accurately: the screening sets the restriction, the restriction shows as a code, and ignoring it disqualifies you on the road test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If you fail to wear your glasses if required

question: How soon may an applicant who fails the knowledge or road skills test be tested again?
choices: Not twice within a period of one week
The same day, at a different location
After 30 days
After completing a driver improvement course
explanation: The handbook bars testing twice within a period of one week for applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test, citing §17B-2-6 of the West Virginia State Code. The bar applies to both tests, not just the road test.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test may not be tested twice within a period of one (1) week, in accordance with §17B-2-6, West Virginia State Code.

question: An applicant fails the knowledge test on Monday and tries to retake it at another office on Wednesday. What does the handbook say?
choices: They may not be tested twice within one week, regardless of location
A different office is permitted, since the bar applies per location
They may retake it once the fee is paid again
The bar applies only to the road skills test
explanation: The one-week rule is written about the applicant, not the office, and it covers both the knowledge and the road skills test. Since each knowledge test attempt also carries a $7.50 fee, there is a cost as well as a delay to a rushed second attempt.
