source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Applicants who fail either the knowledge or road skills test may not be tested twice within a period of one (1) week, in accordance with §17B-2-6, West Virginia State Code.

question: What must all first-time applicants complete, and when?
choices: A short DUI awareness course, given upon passing the road skills test
A defensive driving class, before the knowledge test
An alcohol awareness course, before the vision screening
A first aid course, within 30 days of licensing
explanation: The DMV requires all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only licence to complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test. On completing it you receive a card or a stamp on your application showing completion.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The DMV requires that all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only West Virginia driver's license complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test.

question: A driver previously licensed in West Virginia moves back from another state. Does the DUI awareness course apply to them?
choices: Yes — the course must be completed by all out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia, even if previously licensed here
No, because they have held a WV licence before
No, because the course applies only to applicants under 21
Only if their previous WV licence expired more than three years ago
explanation: The handbook says the course must be completed by all out-of-state drivers coming into West Virginia even if they have been previously licensed in West Virginia. Having held a WV licence in the past does not exempt anyone.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: The DMV requires that all first-time applicants for a driver's license or motorcycle-only West Virginia driver's license complete a short DUI awareness course given upon passing the road skills test.

question: Which lane should slower traffic use on an interstate?
choices: The right-hand lane, except when passing
The left-hand lane, to stay clear of merging traffic
Any lane, as long as the speed limit is not exceeded
The centre lane on a three-lane interstate
explanation: The handbook states that slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane except when passing. It repeats the rule later in the chapter, adding that a slow vehicle in the wrong lane forces other drivers into abrupt lane changes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane, except when passing.

question: You are travelling at the speed limit in the left lane of a two-lane interstate with nothing ahead of you. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: Move back to the right-hand lane, which is where you belong unless passing
Stay in the left lane, since you are already at the limit
Stay in the left lane to keep the right lane clear for merging traffic
Move right only if a faster vehicle appears behind you
explanation: The left lane is for passing, and the handbook's instruction is to drive in the right-hand lane except when passing. Being at the limit does not make the left lane yours, and it is the lane discipline rather than your speed that keeps traffic flowing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Slower traffic should drive in the right-hand lane, except when passing.

question: What does the handbook ask of you when trucks and buses are entering an interstate?
choices: Be cooperative and give them extra time and space to adjust to the traffic flow
Speed up so they can merge behind you
Move to the left lane and maintain your speed exactly
Sound your horn to signal that you have seen them
explanation: The handbook says trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns and asks drivers to be cooperative, giving them extra time and space. Their size and weight mean they cannot change speed the way a car can.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Remember that trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns.

question: A loaded tractor-trailer is on the entrance ramp as you approach in the right lane. Which response fits the handbook's guidance?
choices: Give it extra time and space to adjust to the traffic flow
Hold your exact speed and position so the driver can predict you
Accelerate past the merge point as quickly as possible
Move onto the shoulder to leave the lane clear
explanation: The handbook singles out trucks and buses as needing extra time to adjust to traffic patterns and asks drivers to be cooperative with time and space. Using the shoulder is not an option — shoulders are for disabled vehicles only.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Remember that trucks and buses entering the interstate may need extra time to adjust to traffic patterns.

question: Which direction do even-numbered interstates run?
choices: East to west
North to south
Always toward the nearest city
The direction is not indicated by the number
explanation: Even-numbered interstates run east to west, and odd-numbered interstates run north to south. Because the numbering is national, it works as a rough compass anywhere in the country.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Even-numbered interstates run east to west.

question: You join an odd-numbered two-digit interstate. What does the number tell you about its general direction?
choices: It runs north to south
It runs east to west
It is a bypass around a city
It is a spur route into a city
explanation: Odd-numbered interstates run north to south, while even numbers run east to west. Beltways and spurs are indicated by three-digit numbers rather than by odd or even two-digit ones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Odd-numbered interstates run north to south.

question: What does a three-digit interstate number beginning with an even digit identify?
choices: A beltway or bypass around a city
A spur route into a city
A toll road
A route that crosses a state line
explanation: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities, while an odd first number identifies a spur route. The distinction tells you whether the road will take you around a city or into it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities.

question: Which statement about interstate numbering is NOT correct?
choices: A three-digit number beginning with an odd digit identifies a beltway around a city
A three-digit number beginning with an even digit identifies a beltway or bypass
Even-numbered interstates run east to west
Odd-numbered interstates run north to south
explanation: It is the even first digit that marks a beltway or bypass; an odd first digit marks a spur route. The other three statements are exactly as the handbook gives them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Three-digit numbers with an even first number identify beltways or bypasses around cities.

question: Why does the handbook tell you to plan an interstate route in advance?
choices: Because interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart
Because interstate routes change frequently
Because navigation devices are prohibited on interstates
Because exits are unmarked until you reach them
explanation: The reason given is that entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, which makes a wrong turn expensive in time and distance. The handbook pairs this with checking the vehicle, since a breakdown on an interstate is both costly and dangerous.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Since interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, it is important to plan your route in advance.  Make sure your vehicle is in good working condition.

question: Which preparation does the handbook specifically recommend before an interstate trip?
choices: Checking gas, water, oil and tires, including the spare tire
Filling the tank at the last exit before joining
Carrying a printed map instead of a navigation device
Driving the route once at a quieter time first
explanation: The handbook says to make sure your vehicle is in good working condition and lists gas, water, oil and tires including the spare. Its reasoning is blunt: a breakdown on an interstate can cost a lot of time and can be dangerous.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Since interstate entrances and exits are sometimes far apart, it is important to plan your route in advance.  Make sure your vehicle is in good working condition.

question: Where is the first guide sign for an interchange placed?
choices: Well in advance of the point where you must turn off
At the start of the deceleration lane
At the exit gore itself
Immediately after the previous exit
explanation: The first guide sign is placed well in advance of the turn-off, which the handbook says permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly. It exists so you can avoid hazardous last-minute manoeuvres.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On interstates, the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well in advance of the point where you must turn off.  This permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly.

question: You see the first guide sign for your exit a long way ahead. What is that distance for?
choices: To give you ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly
To warn that the exit may be closed
To indicate that the exit ramp curves sharply
To mark the beginning of the deceleration lane
explanation: The handbook explains that the advance placement permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly, and tells you to pay attention to the guide signs to avoid hazardous last-minute manoeuvres. A sharp ramp curve is warned by an advisory speed limit sign instead.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: On interstates, the first guide sign for an interchange is placed well in advance of the point where you must turn off.  This permits ample time to change lanes and exit smoothly.

question: Why does the handbook tell you to pay careful attention to the signs at an interstate entrance?
choices: Because an exit ramp is often next to the entrance ramp, marked Do Not Enter and Wrong Way
Because entrance ramps are often unmarked
Because the speed limit changes at every ramp
Because ramps may be closed without notice
explanation: The handbook warns that an exit ramp will often sit next to the entrance ramp, carrying Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs. Reading the signs is what keeps you from entering the interstate against the traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Often, an exit ramp will be next to the entrance ramp, marked with “Do Not Enter” and “Wrong Way” signs.

question: You turn into what you think is an entrance ramp and see a Do Not Enter sign facing you. What has happened?
choices: You are about to enter an exit ramp that sits beside the entrance ramp
The interstate is closed ahead
The ramp is restricted to trucks
The ramp is a spur route rather than a through route
explanation: Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs mark the exit ramp that often sits next to the entrance ramp. Those signs face you precisely because you are approaching from the wrong direction, which is the error the handbook is warning about.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Often, an exit ramp will be next to the entrance ramp, marked with “Do Not Enter” and “Wrong Way” signs.

question: What does an advisory speed limit sign on a ramp indicate?
choices: That the ramp curves sharply
The minimum speed required to merge
The speed limit of the interstate you are joining
That the ramp is under construction
explanation: Advisory speed limit signs are used on ramps that curve sharply. They are a warning about the ramp's geometry, not about the speed you will need once you reach the acceleration lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Look for any advisory speed limit signs on the ramp.  These are used if the ramp curves sharply.

question: An advisory sign on an entrance ramp shows 25 mph. What does it tell you, and what happens next?
choices: The ramp curves sharply, so slow for the curve — you will still need to accelerate to traffic speed before merging
The interstate you are joining has a 25 mph limit
You must merge at 25 mph
You must maintain 25 mph until the end of the acceleration lane
explanation: The advisory speed addresses a sharp ramp curve. Once through it, the handbook's merging steps still apply: find a gap and adjust your speed to meet it so you are travelling the same speed as traffic when you merge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Look for any advisory speed limit signs on the ramp.  These are used if the ramp curves sharply.

question: At what point on the entrance ramp should you begin the merging steps?
choices: About halfway along the ramp
At the very start of the ramp
At the end of the acceleration lane
Once you are level with traffic
explanation: The handbook says that about halfway on the entrance ramp you start taking the steps: checking interstate traffic, signalling, looking for a gap and adjusting your speed to meet it. Starting at that point leaves enough ramp to actually reach traffic speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: About halfway on the entrance ramp, start taking these steps:

question: Which sequence matches the handbook's merging steps?
choices: Check interstate traffic, use your turn signal, look for a gap, adjust your speed to meet it, then merge at the speed of traffic
Stop at the end of the ramp, wait for a gap, then accelerate into it
Signal, move left immediately, then match the speed of traffic
Accelerate to the limit first, then look for a gap as you merge
explanation: The handbook's order is check, signal, find a gap, adjust speed to the gap, then merge travelling at the same speed as other traffic. It also warns not to cut sharply left — follow the lane, merge, and only then change lanes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: About halfway on the entrance ramp, start taking these steps:

question: How does the handbook tell you to check interstate traffic while on the entrance ramp?
choices: With quick glances over your shoulder and to the side
By relying on your side mirror alone
By turning your head and holding the look until a gap appears
By watching the traffic in your rear view mirror only
explanation: The instruction is quick glances over your shoulder and to the side, while also watching the vehicles ahead of you entering the acceleration lane. Quick is the operative word — a long look away from the ramp ahead is its own hazard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

question: Why does the handbook pair shoulder glances with watching the vehicles in front of you on the ramp?
choices: Because a vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane may slow or stop without warning
Because the vehicle ahead will signal the gap you should use
Because you must merge in the same order you entered the ramp
Because the vehicle ahead shows where the acceleration lane ends
explanation: The handbook tells you to be prepared to adjust your driving if the vehicle ahead in the acceleration lane slows or stops without warning. Your attention has to be split between the traffic you are joining and the car immediately in front of you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Take quick glances over your shoulder and to the side.

question: What does the handbook say about stopping on an entrance ramp or acceleration lane?
choices: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane
Stop if you cannot immediately see a gap
Stop only if a vehicle ahead of you has stopped
Stop at the end of the acceleration lane and wait to be let in
explanation: The instruction is plain: do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane. Entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous, which is why the handbook treats stopping as something to avoid rather than a normal part of merging.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane.

question: Traffic looks heavy as you reach the middle of the entrance ramp. Which response follows the handbook?
choices: Keep moving, find a gap, and adjust your speed to meet it
Stop at the end of the acceleration lane until a large gap appears
Stop on the ramp and signal for another driver to let you in
Cut sharply left into the first available space
explanation: Stopping on the ramp or acceleration lane is ruled out, and so is cutting sharply left — the handbook says to follow the lane, merge with traffic, and then change lanes. Matching your speed to a gap is the technique it actually prescribes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop on the ramp or acceleration lane.

question: If no gap in traffic is available by the end of the acceleration lane, what does the handbook allow?
choices: Driving onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stopping, as a last resort
Stopping in the acceleration lane until a gap appears
Reversing back down the ramp
Merging anyway and expecting traffic to make room
explanation: The handbook permits using the shoulder beyond the acceleration lane and stopping, but calls it a last resort because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous. Stopping in the acceleration lane itself is expressly ruled out.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop

question: Why does the handbook treat the shoulder stop as a last resort rather than a normal option?
choices: Because entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous
Because the shoulder is reserved for emergency vehicles
Because stopping there always requires a police report
Because the shoulder is too narrow to hold a vehicle
explanation: The reason given is that entering the traffic stream from a stop is hazardous — you have no speed to work with and must accelerate into live traffic. The shoulder is otherwise reserved for disabled vehicles, which is a separate rule in the same chapter.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: it may be necessary to drive onto the shoulder beyond the end of the acceleration lane and stop

question: Who has the right-of-way when you are entering an interstate?
choices: Traffic already on the interstate
The merging vehicle, because it has less room
Whichever vehicle reaches the merge point first
Neither — right-of-way is decided by the ramp signs
explanation: Traffic on the interstate has the right-of-way, and the handbook adds that you cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room. Merging safely is the entering driver's responsibility.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

question: A driver assumes the car in the right lane will move over to let them merge. Why is that assumption dangerous?
choices: Because you cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room
Because moving over is illegal for the driver already on the interstate
Because right-of-way at a merge always belongs to the entering vehicle
Because the other driver cannot legally change lanes near a ramp
explanation: The handbook explicitly warns against relying on other drivers to see you or make room. That is why the merging steps focus on what you control — your timing, your gap and your speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You cannot always count on other drivers seeing you or moving over to give you room to enter.

question: When should you signal and move into the lane for your exit?
choices: Well before you have to exit
As you reach the exit gore
Once you are in the deceleration lane
Only if other traffic is present
explanation: The handbook says to signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit, because changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash. The advance guide signs exist to make that possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit.  Changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash.

question: Which statement about changing lanes for an exit is NOT correct?
choices: A last-moment lane change is acceptable if you signal clearly
Signalling and moving over well before the exit is what the handbook asks
A last-moment change risks missing your exit
A last-moment change risks causing a crash
explanation: Signalling does not cure a late lane change; the handbook names both risks it creates — missing the exit and causing a crash. The remedy it gives is position, not indication.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Signal and move into the lane well before you have to exit.  Changing lanes at the last moment risks missing your exit or causing a crash.

question: Where should you slow down for an exit?
choices: In the deceleration lane, braking gently to the posted exit ramp limit
On the interstate, well before the exit
On the exit ramp itself, after leaving the deceleration lane
Anywhere, as long as you use your brake lights
explanation: Most exits have a special lane for slowing down, and the handbook says never to slow down on the interstate. Wait until you are in the deceleration lane, then brake gently until your speed matches the posted exit ramp limit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Most interstate exits have a special lane for you to slow down in before you reach the exit ramp.  Never slow down on the interstate.

question: A driver begins braking half a mile before the exit while still in the through lane. What is wrong with that?
choices: Never slow down on the interstate — the deceleration lane exists for that
Nothing, provided the brake lights work
Braking early is correct but should be harder
It is only a problem if traffic is following closely
explanation: Slowing in a live lane puts you far below the speed of traffic behind you, which the chapter identifies as creating a hazard and forcing abrupt lane changes. The deceleration lane is provided so speed can be shed out of the traffic stream.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Most interstate exits have a special lane for you to slow down in before you reach the exit ramp.  Never slow down on the interstate.

question: What are interstate shoulders for?
choices: Disabled vehicles only
Short rest stops on long journeys
Changing drivers and checking directions
Any stop of under five minutes
explanation: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles. The handbook names changing drivers and reading a map as things to do in a rest area or after exiting, not on the shoulder.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles.  Do not use the shoulders for changing drivers, reading a map, or other non emergency purposes.

question: You want to swap drivers on a long interstate trip. Where does the handbook say to do it?
choices: In a rest area or after exiting the interstate
On the shoulder, with the four-way flashers on
In the exit gore, which is out of the traffic lane
Anywhere on the shoulder where visibility is good
explanation: Changing drivers is specifically named as a non-emergency use the shoulder is not for; those activities belong in a rest area or after exiting. The gore is worse still — the handbook forbids stopping there because a driver who missed the exit may cross it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Shoulders on interstates are to be used only for disabled vehicles.  Do not use the shoulders for changing drivers, reading a map, or other non emergency purposes.

question: What is an exit gore, and what does the handbook say about it?
choices: The triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp — do not stop in it
The painted area at the start of the acceleration lane — merge across it
The widened shoulder before an exit — park there only in emergencies
The median crossover — use it only to turn around
explanation: The gore is the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp, and the handbook says not to stop in it because another driver who has missed the exit may try to cross it and strike your vehicle. It is a space drivers cut across, not a refuge.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop in an exit gore (the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp).

question: Why is stopping in an exit gore particularly dangerous?
choices: A driver who has missed the exit may cross it and strike your vehicle
It is the narrowest part of the shoulder
Emergency vehicles use it to reach crashes
It is not visible to drivers on the ramp
explanation: The handbook gives exactly this reason: another driver may try to cross the gore after missing the exit. It is the one place on the roadside where a car is most likely to arrive unexpectedly and at speed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not stop in an exit gore (the triangular area between the through lane and the exit ramp).

question: What does the handbook say about U-turns on an interstate?
choices: Never make one — go to the next exit to turn around
Make one only where a paved median crossover is provided
Make one only when traffic is light and visibility is good
Make one only to reach an exit you have just missed
explanation: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate; go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering. The gravel or paved crossovers in some medians are for police and emergency vehicles only.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate.  Go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering the interstate.

question: You miss your exit and notice a paved crossover in the median a few hundred metres ahead. What does the handbook say?
choices: The crossover is for police and emergency vehicles only — continue to the next exit
Use the crossover, since it is provided for turning around
Use the crossover only if you signal and traffic is clear
Reverse along the shoulder to the exit you missed
explanation: Median crossovers are reserved for police and emergency vehicles, and the handbook tells you never to make a U-turn on an interstate. Going on to the next exit is the answer to a missed exit, as it is to almost every version of this problem.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: You should never make a U-turn on an interstate.  Go to the next exit to turn around before re-entering the interstate.

question: What minimum speed does the handbook give for interstate driving?
choices: Do not drive slower than 55 mph unless conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted
Do not drive slower than 45 mph under any circumstances
There is no minimum speed on an interstate
Do not drive slower than 65 mph unless conditions are bad
explanation: The handbook says not to drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted. It sits alongside the instruction never to exceed the legal limit, so the rule bounds you from both sides.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted.

question: Heavy rain has reduced visibility on the interstate and you slow to 45 mph. Does that conflict with the minimum speed guidance?
choices: No — the minimum does not apply when weather or road conditions are bad
Yes — 55 mph is required in all circumstances
Yes, unless a variable message sign has lowered the limit
No, because minimum speeds apply only to trucks
explanation: The 55 mph floor carries its own exceptions: bad weather or road conditions, or a posted lower speed. In adverse conditions the handbook actively tells you to adjust speed so a safe stop remains possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted.

question: Why does driving much slower than other traffic create a hazard?
choices: Because other drivers may be forced to change lanes abruptly
Because slow vehicles use more fuel
Because slow driving is always a moving violation
Because brake lights are less visible at low speed
explanation: The handbook explains that crashes may happen because other drivers are forced to change lanes abruptly around a much slower vehicle. This is the same reasoning behind keeping right and shedding speed in the deceleration lane rather than the through lane.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you drive on interstates at a speed much slower than other  drivers, you create a hazard.

question: Which statement about speed on interstates is NOT supported by the handbook?
choices: Driving well below the flow of traffic is always the safest choice
You should never drive faster than the legal speed limit
Driving much slower than other drivers creates a hazard
You should always drive at a steady speed
explanation: The handbook treats a large speed difference as the hazard, not speed itself, and asks for a steady speed within the limit. Driving well below the flow is the behaviour it warns against, because it forces abrupt lane changes around you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: When you drive on interstates at a speed much slower than other  drivers, you create a hazard.

question: What does the handbook require during adverse conditions on an interstate?
choices: Headlights must be turned on
Hazard flashers must be turned on
You must leave the interstate at the next exit
You must move to the left lane
explanation: Headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions, in accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code. The handbook pairs that with increasing following distance and adjusting speed so a safe stop is possible.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code, headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions.

question: Besides turning on headlights, what two adjustments does the handbook call especially important in adverse conditions?
choices: Maintaining adequate following distance and adjusting speed to allow a safe stop
Using hazard flashers and moving to the right lane
Increasing speed to clear the affected area quickly
Turning on the high beams and sounding the horn
explanation: The handbook says it is especially important to maintain an adequate following distance and adjust your speed to ensure the possibility of a safe stop. Both are about preserving the room and time you need when traction and visibility are reduced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In accordance with §17C-15-2 of the West Virginia State Code, headlights must be turned on during adverse conditions.

question: What should you do if your vehicle becomes disabled on an interstate?
choices: Move as far off the road as possible, turn on the four-way flashers, and get everyone out and well away from the road
Stay in the vehicle with the doors locked and wait for help
Stop in the exit gore where you are more visible
Leave the vehicle in the right lane with the hazard lights on
explanation: The handbook gives three actions together: get as far off the road as possible, put on the four-way flashers, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road. Staying inside a car on the shoulder is what it specifically does not tell you to do.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle  becomes disabled, move as far off the road as possible, turn on your four-way flashers to indicate your vehicle is stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

question: Your engine dies and you coast onto the shoulder. Passengers want to stay in the car because it is cold. What does the handbook indicate?
choices: Everyone should get out of the vehicle and move well away from the road
Passengers may stay inside if seat belts remain fastened
Passengers should stay inside so the vehicle is easier to see
Only the driver should leave the vehicle to set out flares
explanation: The instruction is to get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road. The chapter also tells drivers to be particularly alert for stopped vehicles, which is the reason a car on the shoulder is not a safe place to sit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If your vehicle  becomes disabled, move as far off the road as possible, turn on your four-way flashers to indicate your vehicle is stopped, and get everyone out of the vehicle and well away from the road.

question: Where should flares be placed for a disabled vehicle?
choices: One about a vehicle length behind and another about 300 feet back
Both directly behind the vehicle's rear bumper
One 50 feet ahead and one 50 feet behind
One in the through lane to close it off
explanation: The handbook specifies one flare about one vehicle length behind the vehicle and another about 300 feet back, each placed on the shoulder near the edge of the through lane. The far flare gives approaching drivers warning at interstate speeds.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Put a flare about one (1) vehicle length behind your vehicle and another about 300 feet back.

question: Why does the second flare go about 300 feet back rather than close to the vehicle?
choices: So drivers approaching at interstate speed get warning well before they reach you
So the flare is visible from the opposite carriageway
So it marks the edge of the shoulder for tow operators
So it does not set fire to the disabled vehicle
explanation: At interstate speeds a warning placed close to the vehicle arrives too late to be useful, so the distant flare buys approaching drivers time to react. Both flares go on the shoulder near the edge of the through lane, where they can be seen by traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Put a flare about one (1) vehicle length behind your vehicle and another about 300 feet back.

question: What does the handbook suggest in very dense fog?
choices: It may be better to leave the interstate and use slower roads to reach your destination
Use high beams to see further through the fog
Follow the vehicle ahead closely to keep its lights in view
Stop on the shoulder until the fog clears
explanation: The handbook says that if fog is very dense it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads. Stopping on the shoulder is not the answer — shoulders are for disabled vehicles, and the chapter warns drivers to be alert for stopped vehicles as a hazard.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the fog is very dense, it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads to reach your destination.

question: You are involved in a crash on an interstate in heavy fog. What does the handbook tell you to try to do?
choices: Get your vehicle off the road as far as possible, because leaving it on the road invites further crashes
Leave the vehicle exactly where it stopped until police arrive
Move the vehicle to the exit gore
Drive on to the next exit before stopping
explanation: The handbook says to try to get the vehicle off the road as far as possible, and warns that leaving it on the road until police arrive invites further crashes. In dense fog, a stationary vehicle in a live lane is close to invisible until it is too late.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If the fog is very dense, it may be better to leave the interstate and use the slower roads to reach your destination.

question: What should you do when signs warn that a lane is closed ahead?
choices: Move over to the open lane as soon as possible
Stay in the closing lane until the merge point to keep traffic even
Slow to 20 mph immediately
Use the shoulder to pass the queue
explanation: The handbook says signs will be posted well in advance and that you should move over to the open lane as soon as possible, avoiding a last-minute change. It also tells you to observe and obey special speed limits, traffic control signs and flaggers in work zones.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If a lane is closed, signs will be posted well in advance.  You should move over to the open lane as soon as possible.  Avoid waiting until the last minute to change lanes.

question: Which statement about construction zones on an interstate is NOT correct?
choices: Lane closures appear without warning, so only the merge point signals them
Signs will be posted well in advance of a closed lane
You should move over to the open lane as soon as possible
You must obey special speed limits, traffic control signs and flaggers
explanation: The handbook states that signs will be posted well in advance, which is the opposite of an unannounced closure. That advance warning is exactly what makes moving over early possible rather than leaving it to the last minute.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: If a lane is closed, signs will be posted well in advance.  You should move over to the open lane as soon as possible.  Avoid waiting until the last minute to change lanes.

question: Which five bad driving habits does the handbook identify?
choices: Laziness, impatience, inattention, arrogance and aggressiveness
Speeding, tailgating, drinking, texting and fatigue
Inexperience, poor eyesight, slow reactions, nerves and distraction
Braking late, steering roughly, poor parking, stalling and drifting
explanation: The handbook names these five specifically as the sources of bad driving habits, and asks you to evaluate your own behaviour against them. They are attitudes rather than manoeuvres, which is why they produce many different errors.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Bad driving habits result from laziness, impatience, inattention,

question: A driver weaves in and out of traffic, speeds from stop to stop and tailgates. Which habit does the handbook describe?
choices: Impatience
Laziness
Inattention
Defensive driving
explanation: The handbook describes the impatient driver as one who speeds from stop to stop, weaves in and out of traffic and often tailgates. It notes such a driver may be concentrating hard, yet still disrupts traffic and raises the chance of causing a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Before changing lanes, what does the handbook say you must do?
choices: Turn your head and look behind you, not rely on the mirror alone
Check the rear view mirror only
Sound your horn and move over
Rely on the blind spot monitor if fitted
explanation: The handbook warns specifically against becoming lazy and looking only in the rear view mirror. You are taught to look for other traffic before changing lanes, driving away from the curb, or getting out on the traffic side — and that means turning your head.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Always turn your head and look behind you

question: Which situation does the handbook say requires looking behind you for traffic?
choices: Changing lanes, driving away from the curb, or getting out on the traffic side
Only changing lanes on a highway
Only when reversing out of a parking space
Only when a passenger is in the vehicle
explanation: All three are listed together in the handbook. Opening your door into traffic is included because a door opened without looking is a common cause of collisions with cyclists and passing vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When does the handbook say you should signal?
choices: Before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from the curb
Only before turning at an intersection
Only when another vehicle is visible behind you
Only when changing lanes on a multi-lane road
explanation: The handbook says to always signal your intention before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from the curb, and calls failing to signal a bad habit related to laziness. Combining it with not looking behind could cause a serious crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Always signal your intention before turning, changing

question: Why does the handbook say you owe a signal to the driver behind you?
choices: Because what you do affects them, especially if you slow or stop suddenly
Because they cannot see your brake lights in daylight
Because signalling is only legally required when followed
Because it allows them to pass you safely
explanation: In the tailgating vehicle situation the handbook says you have a responsibility to the driver following you to signal whenever you make a change in your driving pattern, precisely because sudden slowing or stopping affects them most.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: have a responsibility to the driver following you to signal whenever you make a change in your driving

question: You are turning right on red and no cross traffic is coming. What is required?
choices: A complete stop, regardless of traffic
A rolling stop is acceptable if the way is clear
Slowing to walking pace is sufficient
No stop is needed when turning right
explanation: The handbook states you must come to a complete stop at a stop sign or red light regardless of traffic, even when making a right turn. It specifically warns that pressure from following vehicles and the absence of cross traffic may tempt you to only slow down.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: How does the handbook describe the task of driving?
choices: A full-time job with no room for daydreaming or distracting conversation
A task that becomes automatic with experience
Safe to combine with light conversation and scenery watching
Demanding only in heavy traffic
explanation: The handbook says the driver's seat is no place for daydreaming, mental napping, window shopping, scenic viewing or distracting conversation, and concludes that driving an automobile is a full-time job. Lack of concentration means failing to be observant enough to avoid a crash.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: for daydreaming,  mental napping, window shopping, scenic viewing, or distracting conversation.

question: Within what distance must you dim your headlights for an oncoming vehicle?
choices: 500 feet
200 feet
100 feet
1,000 feet
explanation: The handbook requires dimming within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle. The larger distance applies here because high beams aimed at a driver coming towards you cause momentary blindness while both vehicles are closing at speed.

question: Within what distance must you dim your headlights when following another vehicle?
choices: 200 feet
500 feet
50 feet
300 feet
explanation: When following, the handbook requires dimming within 200 feet. Your high beams reflect from the vehicle's mirrors straight into the other driver's eyes, so the rule applies even though you are behind them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

choices: 500 feet when meeting, 200 feet when following
200 feet when meeting, 500 feet when following
500 feet in both cases
200 feet in both cases
explanation: Meeting takes the larger figure of 500 feet, following the smaller 200 feet. A useful way to keep them straight: the head-on case is the more dangerous one, so it gets the bigger margin.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: What does 'overdriving your headlights' mean?
choices: Driving too fast to stop safely within the distance your headlights light up
Using high beams when low beams would do
Leaving headlights on during daylight
Fitting headlights brighter than the law allows
explanation: The handbook defines it exactly this way. If your lights show 200 feet of road but you need more than that to stop, you are effectively driving blind into the space beyond them — the fix is to slow down at night, not to fit brighter bulbs.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: means driving too fast to stop safely within the distance clearly lit by your

question: On an unlit road at night your low beams light about 150 feet ahead, but stopping from your current speed takes about 200 feet. What should you do?
choices: Slow down, because you are overdriving your headlights
Maintain speed, since headlights do not affect braking
Switch to parking lights to reduce glare
Speed up to shorten your time in the dark
explanation: This is overdriving your headlights: you cannot stop within the distance you can see. The handbook's remedy is speed, because your stopping distance is fixed by physics while your seeing distance at night is fixed by your lights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: An oncoming vehicle's headlights are dazzling you at night. Where should you look?
choices: Well in front of your vehicle at the right edge of the road
Directly at the oncoming headlights to judge distance
At your own dashboard until the vehicle passes
At the centre line to hold your position
explanation: Looking directly into oncoming headlights causes momentary blindness. The handbook says to slow down, keep to the right of your traffic lane, and look well in front of your vehicle at the right edge of the road — which keeps you positioned while preserving your night vision.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When it begins to get dark, which lights does the handbook say to use?
choices: Headlights, not just parking lights
Parking lights until full darkness
Hazard lights until full darkness
Fog lights only
explanation: The handbook says it is both the law and a good idea to turn on your headlights, not just your parking lights, when it begins to get dark or any time visibility may be impaired by fog, smoke or extreme cloudiness. Turning them on a little early helps others see you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When is rain generally most dangerous for traction?
choices: At the start of a light rain, when oil, dirt and water form a slippery film
After several hours of heavy rain
Once the rain has stopped and the road is drying
Only when the temperature is near freezing
explanation: The handbook singles out the start of a light rain, when a mixture of oil, dirt and water forms a slippery film on the road. Heavier rain later washes that film away. The condition makes it harder to keep contact on curves and increases stopping distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: a mixture of oil, dirt, and water form a slippery film on the road.

question: At approximately what speed does partial hydroplaning begin in a standard passenger vehicle?
choices: About 35 mph
About 15 mph
About 55 mph
About 70 mph
explanation: The handbook states that up to about 35 mph most tires wipe the road like a windshield wiper, and that partial hydroplaning occurs at about 35 mph. By 55 mph the tires can ride entirely on top of the water.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: partial hydroplaning occurs on the road at about 35 mph.

question: In a severe rainstorm at 55 mph, what does the handbook say happens?
choices: Tires lose all contact with the road, leaving no friction to brake, accelerate or corner
Tires grip normally as long as tread is good
Braking distance doubles but steering is unaffected
Hydroplaning cannot occur above 50 mph
explanation: At 55 mph in a severe rainstorm the handbook says tires lose all contact with the road and there is no friction available to brake, accelerate or corner. A gust of wind, a curve or a slight turn can then create an uncontrollable skid.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: In a severe rainstorm, tires lose all contact with the road at 55 mph.

question: Which measure does the handbook recommend to reduce the possibility of hydroplaning?
choices: Slow down and keep tires properly inflated, replacing them when tread wear indicators show
Increase speed to cut through the water
Brake firmly at the first sign of water
Let air out of the tires for a wider contact patch
explanation: The handbook lists slowing down in rainstorms, on slushy roads or in standing water, and keeping tires properly inflated with adequate tread. Deep treads let water escape from under the tire and can prevent complete hydroplaning at normal highway speeds.

About two feet
At least four feet

Flooded roads are especially dangerous at night
The road surface may have washed away beneath the water
explanation: Two feet of water will carry most vehicles away, according to the handbook — it is the opposite of safe. The other three statements are all made in the handbook, including that flooded roadways are especially dangerous at night when depth is much harder to judge.

question: How should you brake on ice or packed snow?

Firmly and quickly to shorten the stop
By pulling the parking brake
By downshifting only, never using the brake pedal
explanation: The handbook says to always apply the brakes gently and smoothly on ice or packed snow, and to release them at the first hint the wheels are slipping. Locked wheels on ice mean no steering and no meaningful braking.

question: What is the difference between braking with and without anti-lock brakes?

Without ABS you keep steering; with ABS you cannot steer
ABS shortens stopping distance on ice but removes steering
There is no practical difference on ice
explanation: The handbook states that in a vehicle equipped with anti-lock brakes you maintain the ability to steer while braking, but in a vehicle without them you cannot steer unless you pump the brakes, applying and releasing several times until the vehicle is under control.

High beams
Parking lights only
Hazard lights instead of headlights
explanation: The handbook says to use your low-beam headlights in fog or dense smoke, along with reducing speed, staying alert for an emergency stop, and using wipers to clear moisture. High beams reflect off fog back towards you and make seeing worse.

Turn all lights off to avoid attracting other drivers
Leave only the interior light on
Keep driving slowly rather than stopping
explanation: The handbook says that if fog or smoke impairs your vision you should pull off to the side of the road and stop, leave your lights on, and also turn your hazard lights on — so that a vehicle still moving in the fog can see where you are.

Every year
Every six months
Only when the vehicle is sold

The inspection station's number, and it may be moved to another vehicle
Nothing of legal significance; it is advisory only

A 5-minute break every hour, taken in the vehicle
No break is needed if you feel alert

Drive, since concentration improves when emotions are high

That its brake lights are working
explanation: The handbook says you must always be aware that the vehicle ahead may stop suddenly and without warning, and that if you have not allowed enough following distance the result may be a crash. The defence is to stay alert and keep a safe following distance.

Maintain your speed so the pass is predictable
Speed up to shorten the manoeuvre
Move towards the centre line to make your position clear

Many sideswipe and run-off-road crashes result from being passed.

Yes, on two-lane roads only

Pass anyway, as maintaining flow is the priority
Pass on the right instead
Sound your horn to encourage them to speed up
explanation: The handbook's own words are that if you have to speed to pass, you probably do not need to pass. It also notes that passing increases wear and fuel consumption and exposes you to head-on, sideswipe and run-off-road crashes, so a marginal pass is rarely worth it.

You owe no duty to a driver who chooses to follow too closely

The DMV's, through random roadside checks

question: Which statement about safety belt responsibility is NOT correct?
choices: Each passenger is individually responsible for their own belt
The driver must ensure all passengers are buckled
Everyone in a passenger vehicle must wear a federally approved belt
A medical exception may require proof from the driver
explanation: Responsibility is not left to each passenger — the handbook assigns it to the driver. The other three statements are exactly as the handbook puts them, including that proof of a medical condition may be required of the driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: proof of such a condition may be required of the driver.

question: What is the only legal exception to West Virginia's safety belt requirement?
choices: A person 18 years or older riding in the back seat
Any passenger riding in the back seat
Any adult who objects to wearing one
Drivers travelling under 25 mph
explanation: The handbook describes exactly one legal exception: persons 18 years or older who are riding in the back seat. Age and seating position both have to be satisfied — a 16-year-old in the back is still required to buckle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Safety Belts - It is the Law
source.sourceQuote: The only legal exception is for persons 18 years or older who are riding in the back

question: A 16-year-old sits in the back seat of your car unbuckled. Is that allowed?
choices: No — the back-seat exception applies only to persons 18 or older
Yes — the exception covers anyone in the back seat
Yes — belts are required only in the front
Only if the trip is under a mile
explanation: The exception is limited to persons 18 years or older riding in the back seat, so a 16-year-old must be belted wherever they sit. As driver, you are the one responsible for ensuring it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: By how much does the handbook say safety belts reduce the chance of injury or death in a collision?
choices: 45 to 50 percent
About 10 percent
About 90 percent
25 to 30 percent
explanation: The handbook cites 45 to 50 percent. It explains the mechanism too: a belt spreads crash forces over the strongest parts of the body and helps occupants ride down a crash rather than being thrown forward or out of the vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Safety Belts - It is the Law

question: How does a safety belt protect an occupant, according to the handbook?
choices: It spreads crash forces over the strongest parts of the body
It absorbs the entire force of the impact
It works only in collisions below 30 mph
It protects the upper body but not the hips
explanation: The handbook says a safety belt spreads crash forces over the strongest parts of the body and helps occupants ride down a crash. Used properly it also keeps you from being thrown forward or out of the vehicle, and keeps you in position on rough roads.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Where should the lap belt sit?
choices: Snugly over the lower part of the hips
Across the soft part of the stomach
Loosely across the thighs
Above the waist, under the ribs
explanation: The handbook says the lap belt should fit snugly and comfortably over the lower part of the hips, which still allows normal bending of the body. The hips are bone; the stomach is not, which is why a belt worn high can cause injury.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Safety Belts - It is the Law
source.sourceQuote: and comfortably over the lower part of the hips.

question: A passenger tucks the shoulder belt behind their back and wears only the lap belt. Why is that a problem?
choices: Shoulder belts should be worn with lap belts for restraint and protection of the upper body
It is fine as long as the lap belt is snug
It only matters at speeds above 55 mph
Shoulder belts are optional for rear passengers
explanation: The handbook says shoulder belts, which fit across the shoulder, should be worn with the lap belts for additional restraint and protection of the upper body. Tucking it away leaves the head and chest unrestrained.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Under what age must a child be secured in a child passenger safety device in West Virginia?
choices: Under 8 years old
Under 4 years old
Under 12 years old
Under 6 years old
explanation: West Virginia law requires a driver transporting a child under the age of 8 in a passenger automobile, van or pickup truck to secure the child in a child passenger safety device meeting applicable federal motor vehicle safety standards.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: safety device system meeting applicable federal motor vehicle safety standards

question: A 7-year-old is 4 feet 10 inches tall. What does West Virginia law allow?
choices: A safety belt is sufficient, because the child is at least 4 feet 9 inches tall
A child safety seat is still required until age 8 regardless of height
The child may ride unrestrained in the back seat
A booster seat is required until age 12
explanation: The law provides that if a child is under 8 but at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, a safety belt is sufficient. Height is the trigger because a belt only fits correctly, across the hips and shoulder, once the child is tall enough.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which factor lets a child under 8 use an ordinary safety belt instead of a child safety device?
choices: Being at least 4 feet 9 inches tall
Being at least 6 years old
Riding in the back seat
Travelling less than 5 miles
explanation: Height, not age or seating position, is the deciding factor: the law states that if a child under 8 is at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, a safety belt is sufficient to meet the requirement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which vehicles does West Virginia's child restraint law apply to?
choices: A passenger automobile, van or pickup truck not operated for hire
Passenger cars only
Any vehicle including taxis and buses
Only vehicles registered in West Virginia
explanation: The law as quoted in the handbook covers a passenger automobile, van or pickup truck other than one operated for hire, while the vehicle is in motion on a street or highway of this state.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: A driver extends their left arm straight out of the window. What are they signalling?
choices: A left turn
A right turn
That they are slowing or stopping
That it is safe to pass them
explanation: Arm straight out means a left turn. The handbook shows three arm signals side by side: arm pointing down for slow or stop, arm pointing up for a right turn, and arm straight out for a left turn. These matter when turn signals fail, and for cyclists.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which arm signal means the driver is about to make a right turn?
choices: Arm pointing up
Arm pointing down
Arm straight out
Arm waved back and forth
explanation: Arm pointing up signals a right turn. It is easy to confuse with arm straight out, which is a left turn — the bent, upward arm is the one that means right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: You are following a car whose driver puts an arm out of the window pointing down toward the road. What should you expect?
choices: The car is about to slow down or stop
The car is about to turn left
The car is about to turn right
The driver is signalling for you to overtake
explanation: Arm pointing down means slow or stop. Treat it exactly as you would brake lights — increase your following distance and prepare to stop, since the driver may be signalling by arm precisely because their lights are not working.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which pairing of arm signal to meaning is NOT correct?
choices: Arm straight out means slow or stop
Arm pointing down means slow or stop
Arm pointing up means right turn
Arm straight out means left turn
explanation: Arm straight out means a left turn, not slow or stop. Slow or stop is signalled with the arm pointing down. The other three pairings are exactly as the handbook shows them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: An eight-sided sign is reserved for which one message?
choices: No passing
School zone
Stop
Yield
explanation: The octagon is used for stop signs and nothing else, which is why a driver can identify it by outline alone when the lettering is unreadable.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: These eight-sided signs are reserved for stop signs.  These signs mean you must stop completely. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffi  c before moving again.

question: You reach an octagonal sign at a quiet crossroads with no other vehicle in sight. What does the sign require?
choices: Slowing to walking pace and rolling through
Stopping only if a vehicle is approaching on the cross street
Sounding the horn and proceeding
A complete stop, even with no other traffic present
explanation: The handbook says these signs mean you must stop completely; the requirement is not conditional on whether other traffic happens to be there.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: These eight-sided signs are reserved for stop signs.  These signs mean you must stop completely. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffi  c before moving again.

question: Which statement about a stop sign is NOT correct?
choices: A rolling stop is acceptable when visibility is good
You must stop completely
You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians
You must give the right-of-way to all cross traffic before moving again
explanation: The handbook requires a complete stop and then the right-of-way to pedestrians and all cross traffic; nothing in it permits a rolling stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: These eight-sided signs are reserved for stop signs.  These signs mean you must stop completely. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all cross traffi  c before moving again.

question: At a stop sign with a marked crosswalk, where must you stop?
choices: Behind the crosswalk
On the crosswalk
Level with the sign post
Past the crosswalk, in the intersection
explanation: You must stop behind any marked or unmarked crosswalk so that you do not block the path pedestrians are using.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: At a stop sign, you must stop behind any marked or unmarked crosswalk (joining sidewalks on opposite sides of the street).  If there are no pavement markings or cross walks, you must stop before entering an intersection.

question: A stop sign controls an intersection that has no pavement markings and no crosswalk. Where do you stop?
choices: Level with the far kerb line
Before entering the intersection, where you can see traffic from all directions
In the middle of the intersection
Wherever the car ahead of you stopped
explanation: With no markings you must stop before entering the intersection, and the handbook adds that you should stop at a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: At a stop sign, you must stop behind any marked or unmarked crosswalk (joining sidewalks on opposite sides of the street).  If there are no pavement markings or cross walks, you must stop before entering an intersection.

question: You stop behind the crosswalk but parked vans block your view of the cross street. What does the handbook expect you to do next?
choices: Reverse and choose a different route
Sound your horn twice and go
Edge forward to a place where you can see traffic coming from all directions
Proceed, since you already made a legal stop
explanation: The legal stop and the safe stop are two separate requirements: after stopping behind the crosswalk you must still reach a place where you can see traffic from all directions before moving.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.sourceQuote: Stop at a place where you can see traffi  c coming from all directions.

subtopic: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (upside down)
question: A sign shaped like a triangle standing on its point means:
choices: No passing zone ahead
Railroad crossing ahead
Yield the right-of-way
Stop and remain stopped
explanation: The upside-down triangle is the yield sign, requiring you to give the right-of-way to cross traffic or merging traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (upside down)

subtopic: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (upside down)
question: You are on a ramp merging onto a highway and face an upside-down triangular sign. What must you do?
choices: Stop completely at the end of the ramp regardless of traffic
Maintain speed, because merging traffic always has priority
Signal and move across without slowing
Give the right-of-way to the traffic you are merging with
explanation: The yield sign requires you to yield the right-of-way to cross traffic or to merging traffic, so the vehicles already on the highway go first.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.section: Single Message Shaped Signs - Triangle (upside down)
