source.sourceQuote: Within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection

subtopic: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
question: Which of these locations is NOT on the handbook's prohibited parking list?
choices: Within 20 feet of a mailbox served by a carrier using a motor vehicle
A kerb painted white outside a shop
Upon any bridge or elevated structure or in a highway tunnel
In front of a wheelchair ramp or curb cut
explanation: The listed prohibitions include bridges and tunnels, wheelchair ramps and curb cuts, and 20 feet from a served mailbox; the handbook notes a no-parking kerb may be painted yellow, not white.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Prohibited Parking (§17C-13-3, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: Within 20 feet of any mailbox served by a carrier using a motor vehicle for daily deliveries

question: When you park or stop on a grade, you should turn the front wheels:
choices: Straight ahead and rely on the transmission
Away from the curb so the vehicle rolls clear
In whichever direction is easiest to drive out
To the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll
explanation: Turning the front wheels to the curb side of the highway means that if the vehicle creeps, the wheels bring it against the kerb instead of into traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

question: Besides turning the wheels, what else does the handbook require when parking on a grade?
choices: Setting the emergency or parking brake
Leaving the vehicle in neutral
Chocking a wheel
Parking with two wheels on the sidewalk
explanation: You must be sure to set the emergency or parking brake, and the handbook adds that in an automatic you put the selector in park to reinforce it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If you park or stop on a grade, turn the front wheels to the curb side of the highway so the vehicle will not roll.  Be sure to set the emergency or parking brake.

subtopic: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
question: When you have finished parallel parking, your wheels should be within how far of the curb?
choices: 24 inches
36 inches
18 inches
12 inches
explanation: The handbook requires the wheels to be parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb, and the vehicle to face the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: When parallel parking on the left side of the road, wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb.  Park in the direction of the traffic.

subtopic: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
question: You have parallel parked on the left side of a one-way street. Which curb do the wheels have to be within 18 inches of?
choices: The right curb
Either curb
Neither — the 18-inch rule only applies on the right
The left curb
explanation: When parallel parking on the left side of the road the wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb, and the vehicle still faces the direction of traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Parallel Parking (§17C-13-4, W. Va. State Code)
source.sourceQuote: When parallel parking on the left side of the road, wheels should be within 18 inches of the left curb.  Park in the direction of the traffic.

question: The handbook's recommended method for judging following distance is:
choices: Two car lengths at any speed
Half the speedometer reading in feet
The three-to-four second rule
One car length for every 10 mph
explanation: The best way to assure proper following distance is the three-to-four second rule, which stays correct at every speed without any arithmetic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The best way to assure proper following distance is to use the three-to-four second rule.

question: The vehicle ahead passes a bridge abutment and you reach it while still saying 'one thousand two'. What does that tell you?
choices: You have a safe gap
You are following too far back
The test only works at low speed
You are following too closely
explanation: If you reach the fixed object before you finish saying 'one thousand three', you are driving too closely and need to drop back.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

question: Which of these is NOT a suitable fixed object for counting following distance?
choices: The vehicle ahead of you
A signpost
An overpass
A bridge abutment
explanation: The object has to be fixed — the handbook names a signpost, tree, overpass or bridge abutment — because a moving vehicle gives you no reference point.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: To use the three-to-four second rule, choose a fixed object on the road ahead (such as a signpost, tree, overpass, or bridge abutment).  When the vehicle ahead passes that object, begin to count “one thousand one, one thousand two, one thousand three.”

question: If it is dark or raining, your following distance should be at least:
choices: Four seconds
Two seconds
Three seconds
Six seconds
explanation: The handbook raises the minimum to at least four seconds when it is dark or raining, because both sight and grip are reduced.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If it is dark or raining, the distance should be at least four seconds.

question: There is ice and snow on the road. How far back should you stay from the vehicle in front?
choices: The same as in dry conditions
At least six seconds
At least four seconds
At least three seconds
explanation: On ice or snow you should stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front, double the usual dry-weather figure.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

question: A driver is keeping a six-second gap. Which condition does the handbook match to that distance?
choices: Dry daylight driving
Following a motorcycle in the dry
Ice or snow
Dark or raining
explanation: Six seconds is the figure the handbook gives for ice or snow; four seconds covers dark or rain and three to four is the general baseline.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If there is ice or snow, stay at least six seconds behind the vehicle in front.

question: Besides checking your mirrors, what must you do before changing lanes?
choices: Sound your horn
Flash your headlights
Slow to below the speed limit
Check over your shoulder for the blind spot
explanation: A head check over the left or right shoulder is needed because mirrors do not cover the blind spot where another vehicle can sit unseen.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

question: Where does the handbook say you must NOT change lanes?
choices: In an intersection or at a railroad crossing
On a four-lane divided highway
Within 100 feet of a driveway
Anywhere broken white lines are present
explanation: The rule is DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing, both places where vehicles enter your path from directions you are not watching.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: DO NOT change lanes in an intersection or at a railroad crossing.

question: You have checked your mirrors and your blind spot and both are clear. What is the remaining check the handbook lists?
choices: Whether you are exceeding the minimum speed
Whether another driver is also moving into the same lane
Whether your tyres are correctly inflated
Whether the lane ends within a mile
explanation: The handbook adds a check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane — the vehicle converging from the far side that neither mirror nor head check covers.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Check over your left or right shoulder (head check) to make sure no one is in your blind spot.

question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears their front bumper
After counting five seconds
When the passed driver flashes their lights
When you can see the front of the passed vehicle, both headlights, in your rear view mirror
explanation: Seeing both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rear view mirror is the handbook's proof that you have left it enough space to keep braking distance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

question: Passing on the right is:
choices: Not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing
Always permissible on a multi-lane road
Permissible if the vehicle ahead is turning left
Permissible at any intersection
explanation: The handbook says passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Signal and return to the proper lane when you see the front of the vehicle (both headlights) you have passed in your rear view mirror. Passing on the right is not permissible unless there is a lane designated for passing.

question: You are about to overtake on a two-lane highway at night. What does the handbook allow you to do to alert the driver ahead?
choices: Sound a long horn blast only
Blink your headlights
Flash your hazard lights
Use your high beams continuously
explanation: You should sound your horn to alert the driver ahead, and at night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Move left when clear and sound your horn to alert the driver ahead that you are passing. At night you can also blink your headlights to signal that you are about to pass.

subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
question: Passing is prohibited within how many feet of an intersection?
choices: 200 feet
500 feet
100 feet
50 feet
explanation: Passing is prohibited within 100 feet of an intersection, because a vehicle can emerge into the lane you are occupying.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: On a curve or hill or at any place where you cannot see oncoming traffic.

subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
question: Which of these is NOT a place where the handbook prohibits passing?
choices: Within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel or underpass
On a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic
When the solid yellow line is in your lane
On a straight, level road with a broken yellow line on your side
explanation: A broken yellow line on your side of a clear, straight road is exactly where passing is allowed when it is safe; the other three are on the prohibited list.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: Within 100 feet of a bridge, viaduct, tunnel, or underpass.

subtopic: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
question: The car ahead of you has stopped at an intersection to let a pedestrian cross. May you pass it?
choices: No — passing is prohibited in that situation
Yes, if you pass on the right
Yes, if the pedestrian has passed your lane
Yes, if no oncoming traffic is visible
explanation: Passing is prohibited when a vehicle in front of you has stopped at an intersection to allow a pedestrian to cross, because the stopped car hides the pedestrian from you.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Passing is PROHIBITED in the following places
source.sourceQuote: When a vehicle in front of you has stopped at an intersection to allow a pedestrian to cross.

question: You are following a slow vehicle and considering a pass. Which condition must be satisfied first?
choices: The vehicle ahead signals you to go
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic
You can complete the pass within 100 feet
You can reach at least 10 mph above the limit
explanation: The handbook states you cannot pass safely unless you can see far enough ahead, can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle is capable of the speed needed.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.

question: The handbook describes right-of-way as something that is:
choices: Assigned by vehicle size
Held by the faster vehicle
Given, not taken
Earned by arriving first
explanation: Right-of-way is something to be given rather than taken, and if another driver does not follow the rules you are told to give it to them anyway.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, in every situation, right-of-way is something to be given, not taken.

question: You have the right-of-way at an intersection, but another driver pulls out in front of you anyway. What does the handbook expect?
choices: Hold your course, since the rules are on your side
Sound the horn and continue at the same speed
Accelerate to clear the intersection first
Give the right-of-way rather than insist on it
explanation: The handbook is explicit that if the other driver does not follow the rules, you give the right-of-way; being right is no protection in a collision.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, in every situation, right-of-way is something to be given, not taken.

question: When entering a public street from an alley, private road or driveway you must:
choices: Stop only if a sign requires it
Yield to traffic already on the roadway
Proceed, because entering traffic has priority
Yield only to vehicles approaching from the left
explanation: Traffic already on the roadway has the right-of-way over a vehicle entering it from an alley, private road or driveway.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When entering a public street or highway from an alley, private road, or driveway, you must yield to traffic already on the roadway.

question: You are leaving a shop car park across a sidewalk and onto a busy street. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: You, because the car park exit is signed
Whoever arrives at the kerb line first
Pedestrians on the sidewalk and traffic already on the street
You, because you are already in motion
explanation: You must yield to traffic already on the roadway, and pedestrians have the right of way where the sidewalk crosses a driveway entrance.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: They are crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway.

question: At a four-way stop, two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time. Who goes first?
choices: The driver on the left
The vehicle going straight ahead
The larger vehicle
The driver on the right
explanation: At uncontrolled intersections and four-way stops, a driver who arrives at the same time as another vehicle yields to the driver on the right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Uncontrolled intersections and four-way stop intersections - If you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the driver on the right.

question: You arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals at the same moment as a car to your right. What must you do?
choices: Yield to the car on your right
Proceed, since there are no signs
Yield only if it is turning
Sound your horn and proceed
explanation: The same-time rule covers uncontrolled intersections as well as four-way stops: yield to the driver on the right.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Uncontrolled intersections and four-way stop intersections - If you reach the intersection at the same time as another vehicle, yield to the driver on the right.

question: You are approaching an intersection controlled by a yield sign. What does the handbook require before the intersection?
choices: Yield only to traffic already inside the intersection
Slow down before reaching it, then yield to vehicles in it and to approaching traffic
Stop completely at the sign every time
Maintain speed unless a vehicle is visible
explanation: At intersections with yield signs you slow down before reaching the intersection, then yield to any vehicle in the intersection and to approaching traffic.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Intersections with yield signs - Slow down before reaching the intersection

question: When making a left turn you must yield the right-of-way to:
choices: Traffic on the cross street only
No one, if you signalled
Oncoming traffic
Traffic behind you
explanation: A left turn crosses the path of oncoming traffic, which is why the turning driver must always yield to it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When making a left turn, you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.

question: You are turning left and an oncoming vehicle is about to reach the intersection at roughly the same time as you. What should you do?
choices: Turn quickly ahead of it
Turn while sounding your horn
Proceed, since you arrived at the intersection first
Stop until it is safe for you to turn
explanation: The handbook says that if traffic is about to reach the intersection at approximately the same time, stop until it is safe for you to turn.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When turning left, watch for approaching traffi  c in the opposite lane.

question: An ambulance approaches with siren sounding and lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop
Stop immediately wherever you are, including in the intersection
Speed up to clear the road ahead
Move to the left edge of the road
explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights by pulling to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stopping until it passes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: You must yield to any emergency vehicle (ambulance, fire, or police vehicle) that is sounding a siren and flashing warning lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: You have pulled over and stopped for a fire engine. What two things does the handbook tell you to do next?
choices: Move off as soon as its lights are out of sight
Keep your foot on the brake, and watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding
Switch off your engine and wait two minutes
Follow the fire engine to clear the traffic
explanation: Keeping your foot on the brake shows the emergency driver you are stopped, and you should watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding because they often travel in groups.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Keep your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped. Watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding.

question: A police officer is directing traffic and waves you through a red light. What controls?
choices: The red signal, which always controls
Whichever came first
The road markings
The officer's direction, which overrules any sign, signal or road marking
explanation: Directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal or road marking.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Directions of a police officer overrule the message of any sign, signal, or road marking.

question: Which statement about funeral processions is NOT correct?
choices: The law requires you to yield to a funeral procession
Yielding to a procession is a courtesy
Once the lead vehicle has cleared an intersection the rest of the procession has the right-of-way
You may pass a procession on an expressway
explanation: Yielding to a funeral procession is a courtesy rather than a legal requirement, though the procession does hold the right-of-way once its lead vehicle has cleared the intersection.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Although not required by law, it is a courtesy to yield to vehicles in a funeral procession.

question: Pedestrians have the right of way when they are:
choices: Only at signalised intersections
Only in school zones
In a crosswalk
Anywhere on the roadway at any time
explanation: The handbook lists a crosswalk first among the places pedestrians have the right of way, along with a sidewalk crossing an alley or driveway and a blind person crossing with a cane or guide dog.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Remember, pedestrians have the right of way when:

question: A person is walking along the sidewalk and is about to cross the mouth of the driveway you are pulling out of. Who has the right of way?
choices: You, because the driveway is private
Whoever moves first
The pedestrian only if the driveway is marked
The pedestrian
explanation: Pedestrians have the right of way when crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway, which is exactly this situation.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: They are crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway.

question: Why does the handbook demand extreme care near school zones, bus stops, playgrounds and parks?
choices: Vehicle-pedestrian collisions account for nearly 20% of traffic fatalities and those are places pedestrians gather
Speed limits are unmarked there
Pedestrians never have the right of way there
Parking is prohibited there
explanation: Nearly a fifth of traffic fatalities involve pedestrians, and the handbook names school zones, bus stops, playgrounds and parks as places where special hazards exist.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Vehicle-pedestrian collisions account for nearly 20% of traffic  fatalities. Drivers must use extreme care to avoid colliding with a pedestrian, especially in areas where special hazards exist, such as school zones, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks.

subtopic: Sharing the Road with Pedestrians - Pedestrians must
question: Where there is no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk:
choices: On the left side, facing oncoming traffic
On the right side, with traffic
In the centre of the lane
Only after dark with a light
explanation: Walking on the left facing oncoming traffic lets a pedestrian see an approaching vehicle and step clear, which walking with traffic does not.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Pedestrians - Pedestrians must
source.sourceQuote: When walking along a road where there is no sidewalk, walk on the left side facing oncoming traffic. Walk on the shoulder of the road, if possible.

question: Which of these may a pedestrian NOT do?
choices: Obey WALK and DON'T WALK signals
Walk on an interstate highway
Use crosswalks at intersections
Walk on the shoulder where there is no sidewalk
explanation: Pedestrians must not walk on interstate highways or other areas where signs to that effect are posted.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Pedestrians must not walk on interstate highways or other areas where signs to that effect are posted.

question: A school bus ahead stops with its red lights flashing to let children off. Which traffic must stop?
choices: Only traffic behind the bus
Only traffic in the same lane as the bus
Only traffic on undivided streets
Traffic in both directions
explanation: On all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus with its red lights flashing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: On all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads or driveways, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus that has its red

question: A school bus stops with red lights flashing in a shopping centre car park. Do the school bus rules apply?
choices: Yes — the rule covers parking lots, private roads and driveways as well as highways
No, because it is not a public highway
No, because car parks have no lane markings
Only if children are visible outside the bus
explanation: The rule expressly covers all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways, so a car park is included.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: On all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads or driveways, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus that has its red

question: Which statement about stopping for a school bus is NOT correct?
choices: The bus must have its red lights flashing
You only have to stop on public highways
The rule covers parking lots, private roads and driveways as well as highways
Traffic in both directions must stop
explanation: The obligation is not limited to public highways: the rule expressly names all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads and driveways.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: On all highways, streets, parking lots, private roads or driveways, traffic in both directions must stop before reaching a school bus that has its red

question: After stopping for a school bus, when may you proceed?
choices: When the bus resumes motion, the driver signals you on, or the visual signals stop
As soon as the last child leaves the roadway
After waiting ten seconds
As soon as the door closes
explanation: You may not proceed until the bus resumes motion, you are signalled by the school bus driver, or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: proceed until the bus resumes motion, or signaled by the school bus driver to proceed or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

question: The children have left the bus and walked away, but the red lights are still flashing. May you go?
choices: Yes, if you are travelling in the opposite direction
No — the visual signals are still actuated
Yes, because the children are clear
Yes, if you pass slowly
explanation: Until the bus moves off, the driver signals you, or the visual signals stop operating, you must remain stopped — another child may still be crossing.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: proceed until the bus resumes motion, or signaled by the school bus driver to proceed or the visual signals are no longer actuated.

question: On which type of road does traffic coming toward a stopped school bus on the other side of a median NOT have to stop?
choices: Any four-lane road
Roads with a posted limit of 55 mph or more
Interstate highways
Any divided highway
explanation: The handbook gives exactly one exception: only on interstate highways does traffic coming toward a bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Only on Interstate Highways does traffic coming toward a school bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

question: You are on a divided four-lane road that is not an interstate when a school bus on the other side of the median stops with red lights flashing. What must you do?
choices: Continue, because the median separates you
Slow to 15 mph and continue
Continue only if no children are visible
Stop, because the exception applies only to interstate highways
explanation: The exception is limited to interstate highways, so on any other divided road oncoming traffic must still stop.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Only on Interstate Highways does traffic coming toward a school bus stopped on the other side of the median not have to stop.

question: What is the minimum driver's license suspension for a first offence of passing a stopped school bus?
choices: 60 days
30 days
90 days
Six months
explanation: A first offence carries a minimum 60-day driver's license suspension, together with a minimum $500 fine or confinement in jail for not more than six months.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The penalty for passing a stopped school bus is a minimum of 60 days driver’s license suspension and a minimum fine of $500 or confinement in jail for not more than six (6) months for the first offense.

question: Which statement about the penalty for passing a stopped school bus is NOT correct?
choices: If the driver cannot be identified, the owner or lessee may be guilty of a misdemeanor
Subsequent offences carry the same penalty as the first
The minimum fine for a first offence is $500
The minimum licence suspension for a first offence is 60 days
explanation: The handbook states that subsequent offences have increased penalties, so they are not treated the same as a first offence.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The penalty for passing a stopped school bus is a minimum of 60 days driver’s license suspension and a minimum fine of $500 or confinement in jail for not more than six (6) months for the first offense.

question: You must dim your headlights within how many feet of an approaching vehicle?
choices: 500 feet
200 feet
300 feet
1,000 feet
explanation: High beams must be dimmed within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle so you do not blind the oncoming driver.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Dim your headlights within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle.

question: You must dim your headlights within how many feet of the vehicle in front of you?
choices: 300 feet
200 feet
500 feet
100 feet
explanation: Following another vehicle, dim within 200 feet, because your high beams reflect off their mirrors into their eyes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Dim your headlights within 200 feet of the vehicle in front of you.

question: A vehicle is approaching with its high beams on and you are dazzled. What does the handbook say to do?
choices: Close one eye until it passes
Brake hard and stop
Look toward the right edge of the road instead of at the lights
Switch your own high beams on to match
explanation: Avoid looking directly into the lights of oncoming vehicles by looking toward the right edge of the road, which keeps you on course while your eyes recover.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Avoid looking directly into the lights of oncoming vehicles by looking toward the right edge of the road.

question: Headlights must be turned on:
choices: From sunset to sunrise, and whenever people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at 500 feet
Only between midnight and dawn
Only when it is fully dark
Only when other drivers flash you
explanation: The rule covers sunset to sunrise plus fog, smoke or rain, and any other time people and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at a distance of 500 feet.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Turn on your headlights from sunset to sunrise, during fog, smoke, rain, or at any other time when persons and vehicles cannot be seen clearly at a distance of 500 feet.

question: You are driving into thick fog in the middle of the afternoon. Which lights should you use?
choices: Hazard lights only
Low beams
High beams
Parking lights
explanation: Use low beam lights when driving in fog, because high beams cause the light to be reflected back into your eyes.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Use low beam lights when driving in fog. High beams cause the light to be reflected back into your eyes.

question: Which of these uses of lights is NOT correct?
choices: Turning headlights on during smoke or rain
Keeping headlights and taillights properly adjusted and cleaned
Driving on parking lights in light rain
Using low beams in fog
explanation: Parking lights are to be used only when you are parked; rain calls for headlights.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Use your parking lights only when you are parked.

question: A vehicle is following you too closely. What is the first step the handbook gives?
choices: Tap your brakes gently to flash the brake lights
Accelerate to open the gap
Brake hard to warn them
Move into the left lane
explanation: Tapping the brakes gently flashes the brake lights and warns the tailgater without the risk of a hard brake application in front of them.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Tap your brakes gently to flash the brake lights and warn the tailgater.

question: Flashing your brake lights has not worked and the driver is still tailgating you. What should you do next?
choices: Straddle the lane line to block them
Slow down to encourage them to pass, and if that fails pull over and let them by
Speed up until they fall behind
Brake hard to force them back
explanation: The handbook's sequence is to slow down to encourage the vehicle to pass, and if all else fails, pull over, stop and let it pass.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: If all else fails, pull over, stop and let the vehicle pass.

question: How much of a lane is a motorcyclist entitled to?
choices: The entire lane
Half the lane
Only the right-hand portion
Only as much as the rider is using at that moment
explanation: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to manoeuvre around hazards and traffic situations, so you must never share a lane with one.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

question: The motorcyclist ahead of you moves from one side of the lane to the other. What should you conclude?
choices: The rider has lost control
This is normal — riders move around in the lane to handle hazards
The rider is inviting you to pass in the same lane
The rider is about to turn
explanation: Motorists should expect to see motorcyclists move around in their lane, because the rider needs the whole width to avoid road hazards.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

question: What minimum following distance does the handbook suggest behind a motorcycle?
choices: One second, since motorcycles are short
Six seconds at all times
Three to four seconds, increased at night and in bad weather
Two seconds in all conditions
explanation: It is wise to keep a safe minimum three-to-four second following distance behind a motorcycle and to increase it at night and under adverse weather conditions.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Motorcyclists are entitled to and will need the entire lane to maneuver around possible hazards and traffic situations.  It is wise to keep a safe minimum three -to-four second following distance.

question: When passing a motorcycle you should:
choices: Stay in your lane and use the left half
Go all the way into the other lane
Share the lane and pass alongside
Pass on the right shoulder
explanation: Go all the way into the other lane: besides having the legal right to an entire lane, the rider may need to swerve to avoid something on the road.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Stay farther back than if you were behind a vehicle.  The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can.  When passing, go all the way into the other lane.

question: Why does the handbook tell you to stay farther back behind a motorcycle than behind a car?
choices: Motorcycles have no brake lights
Motorcycles are required to stop at every intersection
The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can
Motorcycles accelerate more slowly
explanation: A motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than the vehicle behind it, so the normal car-following gap is not enough.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Stay farther back than if you were behind a vehicle.  The motorcycle can usually slow or stop much faster than you can.  When passing, go all the way into the other lane.

question: You have just overtaken a motorcycle. When should you move back?
choices: As soon as your rear bumper clears it
Immediately, to reduce time in the other lane
When the rider flashes their headlight
Once you are well down the road
explanation: Once you have passed, wait until you are well down the road before moving back into the other lane, so you do not cut into the rider's braking space.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Once you have passed, wait until you are well down the road before moving back into the other lane.

subtopic: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer travelling 55 mph needs how much distance to stop compared with a car?
choices: Half again as much
Twice the distance
Three times the distance
The same distance
explanation: A fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph needs three times the distance a car needs to stop, which is why the space in front of one is not yours to take.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
source.sourceQuote: A fully loaded tractor-trailer, traveling 55 mph, needs three (3) times the distance a vehicle needs to stop.

question: Your exit is approaching and you have just passed a loaded truck. What is the risk in cutting straight back in front of it?
choices: The truck cannot change lanes
You may damage the truck's mirrors
The truck will be unable to signal
You take away the distance the truck needs to stop
explanation: A loaded truck needs three times a car's stopping distance, so moving into that space leaves it no room to stop if traffic slows; the handbook says never to cut off a truck to reach your exit.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: Never cut off a truck in traffic or on the highway to reach your exit or turn.

question: The No-Zone around a heavy truck refers to:
choices: The area directly in front of the truck's bumper only
A lane reserved for trucks
The distance a truck needs to turn
The truck's blind spots, where the driver cannot see you
explanation: The No-Zone is the truck's blind spots, which are dangerous because truck drivers cannot see vehicles in those areas.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The easiest way to avoid lingering in the “No-Zone” is to look for the truck driver’s reflection in the side mirror. If you cannot see the driver’s reflection, you are in the truck driver’s blind spot.

question: How can you tell whether you are in a truck's blind spot?
choices: If you cannot see the driver's reflection in the side mirror
If you cannot see the truck's rear doors
If the truck's headlights are not visible
If you are within two car lengths
explanation: The easiest test is to look for the truck driver's reflection in the side mirror: if you cannot see the driver's reflection, you are in the blind spot.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: The easiest way to avoid lingering in the “No-Zone” is to look for the truck driver’s reflection in the side mirror. If you cannot see the driver’s reflection, you are in the truck driver’s blind spot.

subtopic: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
question: Which statement about heavy trucks is NOT correct?
choices: Heavy trucks typically weigh 80,000 pounds
Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars because the driver sits higher
Trucks are longer, heavier and need more room to turn
Trucks have larger blind spots than vehicles
explanation: Trucks have larger blind spots than cars, and typically the larger the vehicle the larger the blind spots.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.section: Sharing the Road with Heavy Trucks
source.sourceQuote: Trucks have larger blind spots than vehicles.

question: After passing a truck in dry conditions, how much space should you allow before merging back to the right?
choices: Four seconds
Six seconds
Two seconds
One second
explanation: In dry conditions use the two-second rule and give two seconds before merging to the right after passing a truck.

question: The road is wet and you have just passed a tractor-trailer. How much space should you leave before moving back over?
choices: Two seconds, as in the dry
One second
Ten seconds
At least four to six seconds
explanation: In wet conditions the handbook calls for at least four to six seconds of space, because the truck's stopping distance grows on a wet surface.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: In wet conditions give at least  four (4) to six (6) seconds of space.

question: Which of these does the handbook list under things you should NEVER do around a truck?
choices: Pass a truck on the right during a turn
Give a truck extra room for right turns
Give trucks extra space and time for backing up
Call authorities if you see unsafe truck driving
explanation: Never pass a truck on the right during a turn — a truck swinging wide to turn right will close on anything beside it.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When passing a bicyclist you should:
choices: Pass close so you stay in your own lane
Slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room
Pass quickly to minimise the time alongside
Sound your horn continuously while alongside
explanation: Slowing, making sure the rider knows you are there and leaving plenty of room is the handbook's instruction for passing a bicyclist.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road
source.sourceQuote: When passing a bicyclist, slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room between him or her and your vehicle.  If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing.

question: There is no room to pass a bicyclist safely and a car is approaching from the other direction. What should you do?
choices: Sound your horn so the cyclist moves over
Pass on the shoulder
Wait until the oncoming traffic has gone by before passing
Squeeze past while staying in your lane
explanation: If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing — the room the rider needs does not shrink because you are in a hurry.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

source.sourceQuote: When passing a bicyclist, slow down, make sure they are aware of you, and leave plenty of room between him or her and your vehicle.  If there is no room to pass and traffic is approaching, wait until traffic has gone by before passing.

question: Bicyclists on the road must:
choices: Yield to all motor vehicles at all times
Ride only on the shoulder
Obey the same rules of the road as drivers of other vehicles
Ride facing oncoming traffic
explanation: Bicyclists are expected to know and obey all traffic laws and regulations, the same rules of the road as drivers of other vehicles.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)
source.chapterTitle: Traffic Laws and Rules of the Road

question: Which of these is NOT a duty the handbook places on bicyclists?
choices: Riding in the same direction as other vehicles
Yielding the right-of-way to pedestrians
Signalling turns and stops unless both hands are needed for balance
Riding facing oncoming traffic so they can see it
explanation: Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as other vehicles; walking facing traffic is the rule for pedestrians, not for cyclists.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: A bicyclist ahead of you is riding in a way that looks unlawful. What does the handbook advise?
choices: Give them the benefit of the doubt whether they are operating lawfully or not
Sound your horn to correct them
Pass closely to discourage them
Follow closely until they move aside
explanation: Whether the bicyclist is operating lawfully or not, the handbook tells drivers to always give him or her the benefit of the doubt, because almost any collision injures the rider.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

50 feet
200 feet
500 feet
explanation: Required equipment includes a bell or other device capable of giving a signal audible for at least 100 feet, though no siren or whistle is permitted.

choices: 300 feet
500 feet
100 feet
200 feet
explanation: For riding after dark a bicycle needs a white headlight visible for at least 500 feet to the front, along with a red reflector on the rear.

choices: Brakes able to stop one wheel on dry, level, clean pavement
A bell audible for at least 100 feet
A siren
A red reflector on the rear
explanation: A bell or other audible device is required but the handbook expressly says no siren or whistle is permitted.

choices: Sound your horn
Slow down
Move over to give room
Dim your headlights
explanation: Never sound your horn when approaching or near a horse, as this may frighten the horse and cause a crash.

question: Where may a person riding an animal not go?
choices: Business districts
Interstate highways
Any paved public highway
Roads with a centre line
explanation: Animal riders may use most public highways but they may not use interstate highways.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

None, unless the road is unpaved
The same rights as motor vehicle users, and they are subject to the same rules
Fewer rights, since an animal is not a vehicle
explanation: Persons riding animals have the same rights as motor vehicle users and are subject to the same rules of the road.

question: Must traffic stop for a public bus that is loading or unloading passengers?
choices: No, but you must watch for passengers crossing the street
Yes, in both directions, as with a school bus
Yes, but only traffic behind the bus
Only if the bus has flashing lights
explanation: Traffic does not have to stop for a public bus, but you must watch for passengers crossing the street as they get on and off, and use caution when passing.

question: You are driving through a residential street in the late afternoon. What does the handbook ask of you?
choices: Drive in the centre of the road for a better view
Be extra careful, because it is a place and time where children are likely to be around
Maintain the speed limit exactly to keep traffic flowing
Use your horn regularly to warn children
explanation: Drivers are told to be extra careful in residential areas, school zones and at times and places where children are likely to be around.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 2022, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: An ambulance is travelling behind you in normal traffic. It has no flashing lights and no siren. What does the handbook's rule require?
choices: Nothing special — the duty to pull over applies to a vehicle sounding a siren and flashing warning lights
Pull over to the right and stop immediately
Slow down well below the speed limit and wave it past
Stop where you are, even in an intersection
choiceExplanations: The rule's conditions are a siren AND flashing warning lights. With neither present, an ambulance in normal traffic is simply another vehicle.
Slowing sharply for a vehicle that has signalled no emergency can cause the rear-end collision the rule is meant to prevent.
Stopping in an intersection is the opposite of the instruction: the handbook says to stop clear of the intersection when the duty does apply.
explanation: The handbook attaches conditions to this duty: you must yield to an emergency vehicle that is sounding a siren and flashing warning lights. Those signals are how an emergency is communicated to other drivers. With no lights and no siren, nothing has been signalled, and you drive on normally and safely. Add the lights and siren and the duty applies at once.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which conditions trigger the duty to yield to an emergency vehicle?
choices: It is sounding a siren and flashing warning lights
It is an ambulance, fire or police vehicle, whatever it is doing
It is travelling above the speed limit
It is approaching from behind in any circumstances
choiceExplanations: The vehicle type alone is not the trigger — the handbook names the siren and flashing warning lights as the conditions.
Speed is not the test, and you have no reliable way to judge another vehicle's speed against the limit.
Direction of approach is not in the rule; the signals are.
explanation: The handbook's wording is conditional: you must yield to any emergency vehicle that is sounding a siren and flashing warning lights. Both signals are the way an emergency is established to other drivers, which is why the rule names them rather than naming the type of vehicle.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: A police car approaches with siren and flashing lights while you are stopped at a red light in an intersection queue. What does the handbook tell you to do?
choices: Pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop
Stop exactly where you are, including inside the intersection
Accelerate through the intersection to clear the way
Reverse to create space behind you
choiceExplanations: The handbook specifically says to stop clear of the intersection — a vehicle stopped inside one blocks the route the emergency vehicle needs.
Accelerating through a red light creates a collision risk with cross traffic that may also be reacting to the siren.
Reversing is never given as a response and puts you into traffic you cannot see.
explanation: The instruction is precise: pull over to the right edge of the road, clear of the intersection, and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed. Keeping your foot on the brake lets the emergency driver see that you are stopped, and you should watch for other emergency vehicles before moving off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Why does the handbook say to keep your foot on the brake after pulling over for an emergency vehicle?
choices: So the emergency driver knows you are stopped
To stop the engine from stalling
Because the law requires brake lights at all stops
To keep the vehicle from rolling on a crown in the road
choiceExplanations: Stalling is not mentioned anywhere in this instruction and has nothing to do with it.
The handbook gives no such general requirement; the reason it gives here is communication with the emergency driver.
Rolling is not the stated reason — the brake lights are there to be seen.
explanation: The handbook gives the reason directly: keep your foot on the brake so the emergency driver knows you are stopped. Lit brake lights tell an approaching driver at speed that your vehicle is stationary and will not pull out. It also reminds you to check for a second emergency vehicle before moving off.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: The emergency vehicle has passed you. What does the handbook say to do before pulling back out?
choices: Watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding
Pull out immediately to restore traffic flow
Wait a full two minutes regardless of traffic
Follow behind it to take advantage of the cleared road
choiceExplanations: Pulling straight out is exactly what the warning about further emergency vehicles is meant to prevent.
No fixed waiting time appears in the handbook; the instruction is to look, not to count.
Following an emergency vehicle is not permitted or suggested anywhere in the handbook.
explanation: The handbook closes this instruction with watch for other emergency vehicles before proceeding. Emergencies frequently send more than one unit, and the second one is often travelling faster into a road that drivers have already started to reclaim.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: When may an authorized emergency vehicle exceed the posted speed limit?
choices: When on emergency duty with its warning devices in use
At any time, without restriction
Only on interstate highways
Only between midnight and 6 a.m.
choiceExplanations: The handbook attaches a condition — emergency duty — rather than granting a blanket exemption.
No road-type restriction appears in this rule.
No time-of-day restriction appears in this rule.
explanation: The permission is conditional: authorized emergency vehicles may exceed the posted speed limits when on emergency duty with their warning devices in use. This is the same pattern as the yielding rule — the signals are what establish that an emergency is in progress.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which statement about emergency vehicles and speed limits is NOT correct?
choices: They are exempt from speed limits at all times
They may exceed posted limits when on emergency duty
Their exemption depends on warning devices being in use
Only authorized emergency vehicles may show red or blue flashing warning lights
choiceExplanations: This is what the handbook states, with the emergency-duty condition attached.
Correct as stated — the condition is part of the rule, not an add-on.
The handbook says plainly that only authorized emergency vehicles may have these warning lights.
explanation: There is no blanket exemption. The handbook permits exceeding posted limits when on emergency duty with warning devices in use — an emergency vehicle driving normally is bound by the same limits as anyone else.

question: Which vehicles may display red and/or blue flashing warning lights?
choices: Only authorized emergency vehicles
Any vehicle assisting at a crash scene
Tow trucks and construction vehicles
Any vehicle, provided the lights are not used in traffic
choiceExplanations: Helping at a crash does not authorize a vehicle to display emergency warning lights.
The handbook reserves red and blue flashing lights to authorized emergency vehicles.
There is no such general permission in the handbook.
explanation: The handbook states that only authorized emergency vehicles may have red and/or blue flashing warning lights. That exclusivity is what makes the lights meaningful as a signal — when you see them, you know what they mean.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: You see red and blue flashing lights behind you. What does that tell you, and what makes it reliable?
choices: It is an authorized emergency vehicle — only they may show those lights
It could be any vehicle, since the colours are unrestricted
It is always a police vehicle specifically
It indicates a hazard ahead rather than an emergency vehicle
choiceExplanations: The colours are restricted: the handbook limits them to authorized emergency vehicles.
Fire, rescue squad and ambulance vehicles are authorized emergency vehicles too, not only police.
These are vehicle warning lights, not a hazard warning device placed on the road.
explanation: Only authorized emergency vehicles may display red and/or blue flashing lights, so the signal is reliable. Authorized emergency vehicles include fire, police, chartered rescue squad and ambulance. If those lights are accompanied by a siren, the duty to pull over and stop applies.

question: A blind pedestrian with a white cane starts to cross the road away from any crosswalk. Who has the right-of-way?
choices: The pedestrian — they have right-of-way whether or not they are in a crosswalk
You do, because they are not in a crosswalk
The pedestrian, but only at an intersection
Whoever entered the roadway first
choiceExplanations: The handbook removes the crosswalk condition for this case: the right-of-way applies regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk.
No intersection condition appears in the rule — it covers a highway, street or road.
Order of entry is not the test anywhere in this rule.
explanation: This is the exception most drivers get wrong. Ordinary pedestrian right-of-way depends on being in a crosswalk, but the handbook states that a blind person on foot with a guide dog, service animal, white cane or walking stick has the right-of-way on a highway, street or road regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk or not.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which statement about a blind pedestrian's right-of-way is NOT correct?
choices: It applies only when they are using a marked crosswalk
It applies on a highway, street or road
It applies whether or not they are in a crosswalk
It covers a person using a guide dog or other service animal
choiceExplanations: This is the rule as stated — the right-of-way is not limited to any one road type.
Correct as stated; the handbook says regardless of whether they are in a crosswalk or not.
The handbook names a guide dog or other service animal explicitly.
explanation: The crosswalk limitation is exactly what this rule removes. The handbook grants the right-of-way regardless of whether the person is in a crosswalk, on a highway, street or road, when they are using a guide dog or other service animal or carrying a white cane or walking stick.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Which of these identifies a pedestrian the handbook says has the right of way?
choices: A white or metal cane, with or without a red tip, or a guide dog
A white cane only if it has a red tip
A guide dog only; a cane is not covered
Any pedestrian carrying a walking stick of any colour
choiceExplanations: The handbook covers a cane with or without a red tip — the red tip is not required.
Both a cane and a guide dog are named in the handbook.
The colour matters: the handbook specifies a white or metal cane.
explanation: The handbook lists being blind and crossing with a white or metal cane, with or without a red tip, or led by a guide dog, among the situations where pedestrians have the right of way. The phrase with or without a red tip is there precisely so drivers do not treat the red tip as a requirement.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Besides a blind pedestrian, when else does the handbook say pedestrians have the right of way?
choices: When they are in a crosswalk, or crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway
Only when a crossing guard is present
Only at signalised intersections
Whenever they are within 100 feet of a corner
choiceExplanations: Crossing guards are not the condition given in this list.
The list is not limited to signalised intersections.
No such distance rule appears in the handbook.
explanation: The handbook gives three situations together: pedestrians in a crosswalk, pedestrians crossing a sidewalk that crosses an alley entrance or driveway, and blind pedestrians with a cane or guide dog. The driveway case catches people out because it happens on private accesses rather than at junctions.

question: What is the minimum speed rule on a West Virginia interstate?
choices: Do not drive slower than 55 mph unless conditions are bad or a lower speed is posted
There is no minimum speed on an interstate
Do not drive slower than 45 mph under any circumstances
Do not drive slower than 65 mph unless towing
choiceExplanations: The handbook sets a minimum with conditions attached; it is not unrestricted.
45 mph is not the figure given, and the rule does have exceptions.
65 mph is not the figure, and towing is not the stated exception.
explanation: The handbook says do not drive slower than 55 mph on an interstate unless the weather or road conditions are bad or a lower speed has been posted. Driving far below the flow is treated as creating a hazard, because other drivers may be forced to change lanes abruptly.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Heavy fog has reduced visibility badly on an interstate posted at 70 mph. You slow to 40 mph. Is that consistent with the handbook?
choices: Yes — the minimum does not apply when weather or road conditions are bad
No — you must maintain at least 55 mph at all times on an interstate
No — you must leave the interstate at the next exit
Yes, but only if your hazard lights are on
choiceExplanations: The 55 mph minimum carries an explicit exception for bad weather or road conditions.
The handbook does not require leaving the interstate in these conditions.
Hazard lights are not the condition that makes the lower speed acceptable.
explanation: The minimum speed rule is conditional: it does not apply when the weather or road conditions are bad, or where a lower speed has been posted. This is the same read-the-condition pattern as the emergency vehicle rule — the figure alone is not the whole rule.

source.sourceDocument: West Virginia Driver's Licensing Handbook (Rev. 07/2026, retrieved 2026-09-14, SHA-256 45082246ab6df6c75d0968a680b6a7ad26d334aeb2e547871dea3fd7c7828a7a)

question: Why does the handbook treat driving much slower than surrounding traffic as dangerous?
choices: Other drivers may be forced to change lanes abruptly
It uses significantly more fuel
It is always a criminal offence
Slow vehicles cannot be seen at night
choiceExplanations: Fuel use is not the safety reason the handbook gives here.
The handbook frames this as a hazard, not as a criminal offence.
Visibility is not the reason given for this rule.
explanation: The handbook says that driving on interstates at a speed much slower than other drivers creates a hazard, because crashes may happen when other drivers are forced to change lanes abruptly. That is why it also tells you to keep to the right-hand lane unless passing.

question: You must drive slower than the designated speed on a two-lane road and traffic is building behind you. What does the handbook say to do?
choices: Pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster traffic pass
Maintain your speed and let them overtake when they can
Speed up to the designated speed regardless of conditions
Move onto the shoulder and continue driving there
choiceExplanations: The handbook puts the duty on you to let them past, not on them to find a gap.
The rule assumes there is a reason you cannot safely drive faster.
Driving along the shoulder is not what the handbook asks for — it says pull off at a turnout.
explanation: The handbook says that if you must drive slower than the designated speed, pull off at the first safe turnout to let faster moving traffic pass. It applies where the road has one lane in each direction and overtaking traffic has no clear lane for passing.

question: When driving slower than the normal speed of traffic, where should you position your vehicle?
choices: As close as possible to the right edge of the road
In the centre of your lane at all times
Toward the centre line so you can be seen
In whichever lane has least traffic
choiceExplanations: The handbook is more specific than staying centred — it asks you to keep right.
Moving toward the centre line makes overtaking harder, which is the opposite of the intent.
Lane choice by traffic volume is not the rule given here.
explanation: The handbook says that when you drive at less than the normal speed of traffic you should drive as close as possible to the right edge of the road. Keeping right gives faster traffic room and reduces the pressure that leads to risky overtaking.
